[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 11:20-30</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE KING’S WARNINGS, REJOCINGS, AND INVITATIONS</sty>

[BODY] The wonderful portion of Scripture which makes up the rest of this chapter deals with three things, about which there has been great disputing: namely, the responsibility of man, the sovereign election of God, and the free invitations of the gospel. They are all here in happy combination.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">20.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not.</sty>

[BODY] Some cities were more favored with the Lord’s presence than others, and therefore he looked for more from them. These cities ought to have repented, or Christ would not have upbraided them: repentance is a duty. The more men hear and see of the Lord’s work, the greater is their obligation to repent. Where most is given most is required. Men are responsible for the way in which they treat the Lord Jesus and “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">his mighty works.</sty>”

[BODY] There is a time for upbraiding: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Then began he.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>The most loving preacher will see cause for complaining of his impenitent hearers: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">HE upbraids,  </sty>even he who also wept. Repentance is what we who are preachers drive at; and where we do not see it, we are sore troubled. Our trouble is not that our hearers did not applaud our ability, but <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">because they repented not.  </sty>They have enough to repent of, and without repentance woe is upon them, and therefore we mourn that they do not repent.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">21.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.</sty>

--- PAGE 167 ---

[BODY] Jesus knew what the doom of certain Jewish towns would be; and he knew what certain heathen cities would have done if they had been placed in their favorable circumstances.

[BODY] He spoke infallibly. Great privileges were lost on <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Chorazin  </sty>and <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Bethsaida,  </sty>but would have been effectual had they been granted to <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Tyre and Sidon.  </sty>According to our Lord’s declaration, God gave the opportunity where it was rejected. and it was not given where it would have been accepted. This is true, but how mysterious! The practical point was the guilt of these favored cities, in that they remained unmoved by visitation which would have converted the heathen Sidonians; yes, and would have made them repent quickly “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">long ago</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">;  </sty>and in the most humiliating manner, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">in sackcloth and ashes.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>It is a sad fact that our impenitent hearers do despite to a grace which would have brought cannibals to the Savior’s feet!

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">22.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of Judgment, than for you.</sty>

[BODY] Terrible as the hell of these two sinful cities will be, their punishment will be <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">more bearable  </sty>than the sentence passed on cities of Galilee where Jesus taught and wrought miracles of love. The sin is in proportion to the light. Those who perish with salvation sounding in their ears perish with a vengeance. Assuredly the day of judgment will be notable for surprises. Who would have thought to see Bethsaida sink lower than Sidon? Believers will not in <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the day of judgment  </sty>be surprised, for they will remember in that day our Lord’s “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">I say unto you.</sty>”

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">23.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.</sty>

[BODY] The warning to <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Capernaum  </sty>is<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>if possible, still more emphatic, for <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Sodom  </sty>was actually destroyed by fire from heaven. --- PAGE 168 ---

[BODY] and yet it remained unmoved. Those foul sinners of the accursed Sodom, had they beheld the miracles of Christ, would have so forsaken their sins that their city would have been spared. May none of our favored English race perish in the same condemnation! Alas, how much we fear that millions of them will do so!

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">24.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment than for thee.</sty>

[BODY] What <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Sodom will  </sty>endure when the great Judge of all appoints the doom of the wicked, we may not try to realize; but it will be somewhat less than the penalty inflicted upon those who have sinned against the light, and rejected the testimony of the Lord from heaven. To reject the gospel of the Son of God-is to create for one’s self a sevenfold hell. Here, again, our Lord speaks from his own full authority, with “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">I say unto you.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>He speaks what he knows: he will himself be the Judge.

[BODY] So far our Lord spake in heaviness of heart; but his brow cleared when he came to the glorious doctrine of election in the next verse.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">25, 26.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  At that time Jesus answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes. [BODY] He turned to the other-side of truth. “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Jesus answered</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">:  </sty>one doctrine answers to another: sovereign grace is the answer to abounding guilt. With rejoicing spirit Jesus sees how sovereign grace meets the unreasonable aboundings of human sin, and chooses out its own, according to the good pleasure of the Father’s will. Here is the spirit in which to regard the electing grace of God: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">I thank thee.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>It is cause for deepest gratitude. Here is the author of election: “O <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Father.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>It is the Father who makes the choice, and reveals the blessings. Here is his right to act as he does: he is

--- PAGE 169 ---

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Lord of heaven and earth.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Who shall question the good pleasure of his will? Here we see the objects of election, under both aspects; the chosen and the passed-over. <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Babes  </sty>see because sacred truths are revealed to them, and not otherwise. They are weak and inexperienced. They are simple and unsophisticated. They can cling and trust, and cry, and love; and to such the Lord opens up the treasures of wisdom. The objects of divine choice are such as these. Lord, let me be one among them! The truths of the heavenly kingdom are <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">hid,  </sty>by a judicial act of God, from men who, in their own esteem, are “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the wise and prudent.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They cannot see, because they trust their own dim light, and will not accept the light of God.

[BODY] Here we see, also, the reason of election, the divine will: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">So it seemed good in thy sight.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>We can go no further than this. [BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">27.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knoweth the Son, but the Father; neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.</sty>

[BODY] Here we have the channel through which electing love works towards men: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">All things are delivered unto me of my Father.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>All things are put into the Mediator’s hands; fit hands both towards God and towards man; for he alone knows both to perfection. Know Christ, and you know the Father, and know that the Father himself loveth you. There is no other way of knowing the Father but through the Son. In this our Lord rejoiced; for his office of Mediator is dear to him, and he loves to be the way of communication between the Father whom he loves, and the people whom he loves for the Father’s sake.

[BODY] Observe the intimate fellowship between the Father and the Son, and how

--- PAGE 170 ---

[BODY] they know each other as none else ever can. Oh, to see all things in Jesus by the Father’s appointment, and so to find the Father’s love and grace in finding Christ.

[BODY] My soul, there are great mysteries here! Enjoy what thou canst not explain.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">28.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Come unto me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.</sty>

[BODY] Here is the gracious invitation of the gospel in which the Savior’s tears and smiles were blended, as in a covenant rainbow of promise.

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Come”;  </sty>he drives none away: he calls them to himself. His favorite word is “Come.” Not, — go to Moses, “Come <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">unto me.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>To Jesus himself we must come, by a personal trust. It is well to give the largest sense to all that mercy speaks. Jesus calls <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">me.  </sty>Jesus promises “rest”, as his gift: his immediate, personal, effectual rest he freely gives to all who come to him by faith.

[BODY] To come to him is the first step, and he entreats us to take it. In himself, as the great sacrifice for sin, the conscience, the heart, the understanding obtain complete rest. When we have obtained the rest he <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">gives,  </sty>we shall be ready to hear of a further rest which we <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">find.</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">29, 30.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.</sty>

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Take my yoke, and learn</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">:  </sty>this is the second instruction; it brings with it a further rest which we “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">find.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>The first rest he <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">gives  </sty>through his death; the second we find in copying his life. First, we <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">rest  </sty>by faith in Jesus, and next we <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">rest  </sty>through obedience to him. Rest from fear is followed by rest

--- PAGE 171 ---

[BODY] from the turbulence of inward passion, and the drudgery of self. We are not only to bear a yoke, but his yoke; and we are not only to submit to it when it is laid upon us, but we are to <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">take it upon us.  </sty>We are to be workers, and <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">take his  </sty>yoke; and at the same time we are to be scholars, and <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">learn  </sty>from him as our Teacher. We are to learn of Christ and also to learn Christ. He is both teacher and lesson. His gentleness of heart fits him to teach, to be the illustration of his own teaching, and to work in us his great design. If we can become as he is, we shall rest as he does. We shall not only rest from the guilt of sin — this he gives us; but we shall rest in the peace of holiness, which we find through obedience to him. It is the heart which makes or mars the rest of the man. Lord, make us “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">lowly in heart</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>and we shall be restful of heart.

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Take my yoke.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>The yoke in which we draw with Christ must needs be a happy one; and the burden which we carry <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">for  </sty>him is a blessed one. We rest in the fullest sense when we serve, if Jesus is the Master. We are unloaded by bearing his burden; we are rested by running on his errands.

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Come unto me</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">, is  </sty>thus a divine prescription, curing our ills by the pardon of sin through our Lord’s sacrifice, and causing us the greatest peace by sanctifying us to his service.

[BODY] Oh for grace to be always coming to Jesus, and to be constantly inviting others to do the same! Always free, yet always bearing his yoke; always having the rest once given, yet always finding more: this is the experience of those who come to Jesus always, and for everything. Blessed heritage; and it is ours!

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 12:1-13</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">OUR KING AS LORD OF THE SABBATH</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">1.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1"> </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">AT that time Jesus went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungered, and began, to pluck the ears of corn, and to eat. But when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto to him, Behold, thy disciples do that which is not lawful to do upon the sabbath day</sty>

[BODY] They were probably on their way to the synagogue. They were allowed by law to take ears of corn as they passed along; but the objection of the Pharisees was to their doing so on <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the Sabbath.  </sty>Plucking was reaping, rubbing the grain from the husk was threshing, to their hypercritical minds. Their traditions and fancies they regarded as a code of law, and according to this the disciples were doing “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">that which is not lawful to do upon the sabbath day.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They came to Jesus himself with their grave complaints: for once they plucked up courage to deal with the Leader; for they felt very strong on the Sabbath question, and they thought it fair to lay the faults of the disciples at the door of their Teacher.

[BODY] We incidentally learn from this story that our Lord and his disciples were poor, and that he who fed the multitudes did not use his miraculous power to feed his own followers, but left them till they did what poor men are forced to do to supply a little stay for their stomachs. Our Lord bribes none into following him: they may be his apostles, and yet be hungry on a Sabbath.

[BODY] Why did not these Pharisees give them bread, and so prevent their doing that to which they objected? We might also fairly ask, How came they to see the disciples? Did they not break the Sabbath by setting a watch over them?

--- PAGE 173 ---

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">3, 4.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  But he said unto them, Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungered, and they that were with him; how he entered into the house of God, and did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests?</sty>

[BODY] He speaks to his learned opponents as if they had not read the law which they professed to uphold. “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Have ye not read?</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>The instance of David served the Son of David well. It was clear from his example that necessity has no law. The Tabernacle law was broken by David when he and his band were pressed with hunger; and that breach of law touched Jewish ritual in a very special and tender point, and yet he was never rebuked for it. To have eaten the holy bread out of profanity, or bravado, or levity, might have involved the offender in the judgment of death; but to do so in urgent need was not blameworthy in the case of David. As men excuse any breach of manners necessitated by the pressure of hunger, so cloth the Lord permit any ceremonial point of law to give way to his mercy, and to man’s evident necessity. The law of the Sabbath was never meant to compel starvation to hungry men, any more than the law of “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the house of God</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>and “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the shewbread.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Works of necessity are lawful on the Sabbath.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">5, 6.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless, But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple</sty>.

[BODY] This instance is absolutely to the point. <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">The priests  </sty>worked hard on the Sabbath in offering sacrifice, and in other appointed ways; but they were to be honored rather than censured for so doing, seeing they had the approval of the temple law. But in the case of Christ’s disciples, that which they did had the sanction of the temple’s Lord, who is far greater than the temple. Work done for God on the Sabbath is no real profanation of the Sabbath, though it may seem to be so to those whose religion lies wholly in external observances. If we work with Jesus, and for Jesus, we care not for the criticisms of formalists. As the substance is greater than the shadow, so is our Lord greater than the temple, or any or all ceremonial

--- PAGE 174 ---

[BODY] laws; and his sanction overrules all the interpretations of the law which asceticism or superstition may thrust upon us.

[BODY] Works of piety are lawful on the Sabbath

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">7.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.</sty>

[BODY] Our Lord had galled the Pharisees by saying twice, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Have ye not read?</sty>” Did he imagine that they had left any part of the Psalms or Law unread? Now he assails them again with the charge of ignorance of the meaning of a passage from the prophets: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">If ye had known what this meaneth.</sty>” Then he quotes from Hosea 6:6, which he had used against them before. (See chapter 9:13<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">.)  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>There must be very much in this word of the prophet to make it so great a favorite with our Lord. God preferred that his priests should rather give the consecrated shewbread to David as an act of mercy, than keep it sacred to its use: he would rather that the disciples should spend a few minutes in plucking ears of corn for their hunger than suffer faintness in order to preserve the sanctity of the day. Having thus the permit of the Lord himself, those who allowed the merciful act of removing hunger were guiltless, and ought not to be condemned. Indeed, they would not have been condemned had their critics been better instructed.

[BODY] Works of mercy are lawful on the Sabbath.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">8.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">For the Son of man is lord even of the sabbath day.</sty>

[BODY] This sets the whole matter beyond further question. “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">The Son of man</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,</sty> Christ Jesus, being in union with the Godhead, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">is Lord</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>of everything which lies in the range of that law which concerns God and man, seeing he is Mediator; and therefore he may arrange and dispose of Sabbaths as he pleases. He has done so, and has interpreted the Sabbatic law, not with license, but with a sweet reasonableness which the more rigid of religionists do not exhibit. From his example and teaching we learn that the Sabbath is<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>not profaned by works of necessity, piety, or mercy; and that we need not care for the sharp speeches of hypercritical formalists who

--- PAGE 175 ---

[BODY] strain the Sabbatic law, and make a bondage of that which was intended to be a season of holy rest.

[CENTERED] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">9.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue.</sty>

[BODY] The time arrived when the Sabbath question came up again in reference to our Lord’s own work among the sick and diseased.

[BODY] Jesus set the example of attending public worship. The synagogues had no divine appointment to authorize them, but in the nature of things it must be right and good to meet for the worship of God on his own day, and therefore Jesus was there. He had nothing to learn, yet he went up to the assembly on the day which the Lord God had hallowed.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">10. </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And, behold, there was a man which had his hand withered. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse him.</sty>

[BODY] The incident was noteworthy, and therefore it is mentioned with a “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">behold.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>It was remarkable that so very soon a case occurred to bring up again the matter in dispute. Did the Pharisees bring <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the man with the withered hand  </sty>into the synagogue so as to raise the question in a practical form? They went to the synagogue to indulge their bigotry and not to worship: it is to be feared that many in these days imitate then,. Before our Lord made any motion towards a miracle, they were at him with what they hoped would prove an entangling question. “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days?</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>He<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>had claimed to be Lord of the Sabbath; and now they, with much show of fairness, submit a difficulty to him, but it was with a base purpose. In the moral character of questioning, everything depends upon the motive they did not ask that they might learn from him, but<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">that they might accuse him.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They were on the catch; yet they took nothing by their malicious craft.

--- PAGE 176 ---


[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">11, 12.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  And he said unto them, What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold of, it, and lift it out? [BODY] He answers their question by another. He propounds a case, and makes them to be judges in it. If a poor man, with “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">one sheep</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>saw it fall “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">into a pit</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>or become cast on its back “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">on the sabbath</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>would he not “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">lay hold on it, and lift it out</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>and set it on its feet? Of course he would; and he would be right in so doing. <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">How much then is a man better than a sheep?  </sty>therefore it is and must be right to succor a man. Alas, some act as if a man were not better than an animal; for their dogs and horses are better housed than their laborers, and they are more indignant about the killing of a fox than at the starving of a pauper.

[BODY] Our Lord’s argument was overwhelming. One form of human kindness being proved to be right, the whole class of beneficent actions is admitted, and “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>One<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>wonders that anybody ever thought otherwise. But zeal for externals, and hatred of spiritual religion, when united, create a narrow bigotry as cruel as it is ridiculous. Our Lord has set us free from the Rabbinical yoke, and we find rest unto our souls in a true spiritual Sabbath. Let none, however, from this liberty, infer a license, and treat the Lord’s-day as if it were their own, and might be spent for their own purposes. They best keep the Sabbath who on the seventh day, and always, rest from their own works, as God did from his; but how can a man rest until he knows the finished work of God in Christ Jesus?

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">13.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then saith he to the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it forth; and it was restored whole, like as the other.</sty>

[BODY] Thus our Lord practically carried out his own teaching. He that could work a miracle of this sort was divine, and could rightly interpret his own law. The man was sitting down, and Jesus bade him stand up that all might observe him; and then he further bade him hold up his hand so that all

--- PAGE 177 ---

[BODY] could see its lifeless condition. It does not appear that his arm was withered, as some have supposed; but he was able, by the use of his arm to hold out his hand to public view. This being done, the Lord restored it at once, before the whole synagogue, and before the captious Pharisees. The man stretched out each finger perfectly restored to its natural vigor. The poor man had hidden his hand when it was dried up; but when restored, it was meet that it should be seen by all in the synagogue. By that restored hand, made whole on the sabbath, all men knew that Jesus would work deeds of mercy on the sabbath. Let us pray him to do the same in our assemblies. Oh, that the hands which have been useless for holy purposes may at his bidding become whole! Oh, that those who are bidden to believe and live would cease from questioning, and obey, as this man did; then would healing his surely come to them, as it did to the obedient man!

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 12:14-21</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">OUR KING IN THE MAJESTY OF HIS PEACEFULNESS</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">14.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.</sty>

[BODY] The synagogue was too hot for the Pharisees, and so <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">they went out.</sty> Utterly routed, they retire from public gaze, hating the man who had so completely baffled them. Those who begin with seeking to accuse the Lord soon come to seeking to <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">destroy him.  </sty>It was<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>not easy to touch one who lived so much in the esteem of the people, and so they consulted together as to the safest method of procedure. Their killing of Jesus was indeed the result of malice aforethought, for they deliberately, planned their cruel deed. Men at this hour still take counsel “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">against him.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Why<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>and wherefore? [BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">15, 16.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  But when Jesus knew it, he withdrew himself from thence: and great multitudes followed him, and he healed them, all; and charged them, that they should not make him known.</sty>

[BODY] Their secret counsels were all discerned by his omniscience: Jesus <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">knew  </sty>it. He acted accordingly. He came not to contend with cavilers, and therefore <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">he withdrew himself  </sty>from the<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>scene of their perpetual disputations. But he could not get alone; the crowd flocked after him, and his love could not refuse to bless them with healing. He did not want to create an excitement, and so, when the people gathered in multitudes, he commanded them not to advertise his presence. To him popularity became a hindrance in his work, and he shunned it. In this avoidance of notoriety he fulfilled an ancient prophecy.

--- PAGE 179 ---

[BODY] We are under no charge to conceal his gracious wonders, and therefore we would joyfully enlarge upon that glorious record, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">He healed them all.</sty>” What an encouragement to sin-sick souls to bunt in him!

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">17-19.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, Behold my servant, whom I have chosen; my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my spirit upon him, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles. [BODY] It is in Isaiah 42:1-4 that we read words which are quoted in their full sense, if not literally, by the Evangelist. The <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Servant  </sty>of God, elect, beloved, and delightsome to the Lord, clothed with the Spirit of God, would come forth, and reveal the Lord’s mind to the nations; but it would not be with tumult and turmoil, noise and clamor.

[BODY] To avoid contention and ostentation, our Lord quieted those whom he had healed, or at least charged them not to make him known. Our Lord did not aim at raising himself in the esteem of the multitude by successfully contending with the Pharisees; for his method was of another sort. The names given to the Savior here are exceedingly precious, and worthy of our careful meditation, and especially so in connection with the passage in Isaiah. Jesus is the<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  chosen  </sty>of<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Jehovah, ordained to be his servant, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">beloved  </sty>in<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>that capacity, and <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">well pleasing  </sty>to his<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Father. The power of this beloved Servant of God would lie in the divine Spirit, in the doctrine which he would teach, and in the law which he would proclaim; his whole life being a judging and condemnation of sin before the eyes of all men. Not by might, nor by power, but by the Spirit of the Lord, and the force of truth, would he prevail. The wrath of man in hot controversy, the frenzy of wild rhetoric, the torrent of popular declamation; all these he left to mere pretenders: he disdained such weapons in establishing his Kingdom. Certain of his followers have taken an opposite course, and are much enamored of clamorous and blatant methods: in this they will yet find that they are not well pleasing to the Lord.

--- PAGE 180 ---


[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">20.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.</sty>

[BODY] He left <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the bruised raced  </sty>of Pharisaic presence to prove its own impotence, it was not at that time worth his while to break it; and the <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">smoking flax  </sty>of<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>a nominal religiousness he passed by, and left all dealing with it till another day, when the hour should come to end its offensiveness. He will in the end victoriously judge those hypocrites who were useless as bruised reeds, and offensive as smoking flax; but he would not do this during his first mission to men. He is in no haste to destroy every petty opposition.

[BODY] This I take to be the exact sense of the words in this connection; but as the passage is popularly received, it is equally true, and much richer in consolation. The feeblest are not disdained by our Lord Jesus, though apparently useless as a bruised reed, or even actually offensive as a smoking flax. He is gentle, and exercises no harsh severity. He bears and forbears with those who are unlovely in his eyes. He longs to bind up the broken reed, and fan the smoking, flax into flaming life. Oh, that poor sinners would remember this, and trust him!

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">21. </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And in his name shall the Gentiles trust.</sty>

[BODY] Because he is so kind, the despised Gentile dogs shall come and crouch at his feet and love him as their Master. He shall be the hope of those who were left as hopeless. Our Lord’s desire for quiet, and his avoiding antagonism, thus proved him to be the Messiah of the prophets. Shall we not more and more trust in the Anointed of the Lord? Yes, Gentiles as we are, we do trust in <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">his name.  </sty>In us is this prophecy fulfilled Yet how unlikely it seemed that Gentiles would do so when Israel refused him.

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 12:22-37</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">OUR KING AND THE POWERS OF DARKNESS</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">22.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then was brought unto him one possessed with a devil, blind, and dumb: and he healed him, insomuch that the blind and dumb both spake and saw.</sty>

Nothing baffles our Lord. Men who neither see their sin, nor cry for mercy, his grace can save.

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">all the people were amazed!.</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">24.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, This fellow doth not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils.</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">25, 26.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  And Jesus knew their thoughts, and said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand: and if Satan cast out Satan, he is divided against himself; how shall then his kingdom stand?</sty>

[BODY] The Thought-reader meets them with an argument in the highest degree conclusive, overwhelming them by reducing their statement to absurdity. Imagine Satan divided against Satan, and his kingdom thus rent with civil war! No: whatever faults the devils have, they are not at strife with each other; that fault is reserved for the servants of a better Master. Oh, that divisions in the church were not so many, and so desolating as they are! It would be a very hopeful circumstance if we could hear of divisions among the powers of darkness; for then would Satan’s kingdom fall. No, ye cunning Pharisees; your slanderous suggestion is too manifestly a lie, and reasonable men are not to be entrapped by it!

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">27.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? therefore they shall be your judges.</sty>

[BODY] Our Lord here used an argument fitted for the men he dealt with. It was

--- PAGE 183 ---

[BODY] not so forcible in itself as the former one, but as an argument <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">to them  </sty>it would come home with singular force. Some of the disciples of the Pharisees, and probably some of <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">their children,  </sty>acted as exorcists; and, whether truly or falsely, professed to cast out devils. [BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">28.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But if I cast out devils by the Spirit of God then the kingdom of God is come unto you.</sty>

[BODY] Note that, though our Lord had power all his own, he honored the Spirit of God, and worked by his energy, and mentioned the fact that he did so. What can we do without that Spirit? Lord God the Holy Ghost, teach us to wait on thee!

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">29.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Or else-how can one enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house.</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">The devil is the strong man,  </sty>the giant robber. He holds men in possession as a warrior horde his property. Our Lord, when his work began, bound Satan: the presence of God in human flesh was a restraint upon man’s foe. Having bound the enemy, he now takes out of

--- PAGE 184 ---

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">his house  </sty>those spoils which else had been for ever in his possession. There is no deliverance for us save by our Lord’s victory over our powerful tyrant. Glory be to his name, he has bound the mighty, and he takes from him his prey! This was our Lord’s fair and self-evident explanation of the matter concerning which Pharisees theorized so basely.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">30.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">He that is not with me is against me; and he that gathereth not with me scattereth abroad.</sty>

Jesus meant war with the great enemy, and with all who sided with evil. Men would of necessity practically take sides: their actions would tend to gather to him or to scatter from him. Jesus is the one and only possible center of human unity; and whatever teaching does not unite men in him, disperses them through selfishness, pride, hate, and a thousand other disintegrating forces. Our King has thrown down the gage of battle, and he will never accept truce or compromise. Lord, let me never hesitate, but be with thee, and <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">gather  </sty>with thee.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">31.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men.</sty>

[BODY] Here is a solemn warning for these slanderous Pharisees: the sin of reviling the Spirit of God, and imputing his work to Beelzebub, is a very great one; and, in fact, so hardens the heart that men who are guilty of it never repent, and consequently are never forgiven. [BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">32.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.</sty>

[BODY] Why<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>should a word be spoken against Jesus? Yet many words are so spoken, and he forgives. [BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">33.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Either make the tree good, and his fruit good; or else make the tree corrupt, and its fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by his fruit.</sty>

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 12:38-42</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">OUR KING CHALLENGED TO GIVE A SIGN</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">38, 39.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Then certain of the scribes and of the Pharisees answered, saying, Master, we would see a sign from thee. There is need of great patience to deal wisely with such.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">40.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of man he three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.</sty>

[BODY] was full of the power of his resurrection. As Jonah’s ministry was certified by his restoration from the sea, so is our Lord’s ministry attested by his rising from the dead. [BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">41.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.</sty>

[BODY] The heathen of Nineveh were convinced by the sign of a prophet restored from burial in the sea; and moved by that convincement, they repented at his preaching. Jesus came with a clearer command of repentance, and a brighter promise of deliverance; but he spoke to obdurate hearts. Our Lord reminds the Pharisees of this; and as they were the most Jewish of Jews, they were touched to the quick by the fact that heathens perceived what Israel did not understand, and that Ninevites repented while Jews were hardened. [BODY] The standing witness to our Lord is his resurrection from the dead. God grant that every one of us, believing that unquestionable fact, may be so assured of his mission, that we may repent and believe the gospel.

[BODY] RESURRECTION is one proof; in fact, it is THE SIGN; although, as we shall see, it is supplemented by another. The two will convince us or condemn us.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">42.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.</sty>

The superlative excellence of his wisdom stands for our Lord as a sign, which can never be effectually disputed. What other teaching meets all the wants of men? Who else has revealed such grace and truth? He is infinitely greater than Solomon, who from a moral point of new exhibited a sorrowful littleness. Who but the Son of God could have made known the Father as he has done?

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 12:43-45</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">OUR KING UNVEILING THE TACTICS OF THE ARCH-ENEMY</sty>

[BODY] Our Lord was mindful to deal a finishing stroke to the notion of his being aided by Satanic co-operation, by returning to his parable (verse 29), and declaring that, even if the contingency should occur of the evil spirit leaving a man of its own accord, the man would be none the more a subject of hope; for the enemy would return before long.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">43.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and findeth none.</sty>

[BODY] Well is the devil named “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the unclean spirit</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">:  </sty>he loves that which is foul, and makes the man in whom he dwells filthy in heart. In the incident described above, the devil has been in possession “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">of a man</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>and he “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">is gone out</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>for purposes of his own. He has quitted the man of his own accord, without conflict of any kind. This is a case which frequently occurs: the devil does in this way leave the madly immoral to become decent and orderly. The crafty spirit takes the key of the house with him, for he means to return. He has quitted occupancy, but has not given up ownership. He has gone out that he might not be turned out. Who can understand the subtlety of the old serpent?

[BODY] The evil spirit is, however, uneasy when he is not ruling a human mind. He wanders <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">seeking rest and finding none  </sty>He finds nothing to cheer him on this earth, or in heaven, or in hell; these are all <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">dry places  </sty>to him. Within the sinful heart he was at home, and found some little content; but outside in nature he finds a desert for his unclean desires.

[CENTERED] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">“</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">Every prospect pleases And only man is vile!</sty><sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">”</sty>

[BODY] And hence only man affords a suitable lodging for the vile spirit.

--- PAGE 192 ---


[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">44.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then he saith, I will return into my house from whence I came out; and when he is come, he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished.</sty>

[BODY] The foul fiend calls the man, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">My house</sty>.” His audacity is amazing. He did not build or buy that house, and he has no right to it. He speaks of his leaving the man as a mere coming out: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">I came out.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>He says, as if it were an easy matter, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">I will return.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Evidently he considers that he has the freehold of man’s nature, and can go and come at his pleasure. If Satan quits a man of his own will, he is sure to return just when it suits his purpose. Only the divine force which ejects him can secure his non-return. Reformations which are not the work of conquering grace are usually temporary, and often lead up to a worse condition in after years.

[BODY] The unclean spirit carries out his resolve: he returns, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">and when he is come, he findeth it empty</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">:  </sty>no one else has taken possession, and so no one hinders his entrance into his own tenement. It is true it is <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">swept  </sty>from certain grosser sins, and <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">garnished  </sty>with some pretty moralities; but the Holy Spirit is not there, and no divine change has been wrought, and therefore the unclean spirit is as much at home there as ever he was. The parable needs no further explanation; temporary reformation is well pictured. The devil has no objection to his house being swept and garnished; for a moralist may be as truly his slave as the man of debauched habits. So long as the heart is not occupied by his great foe, and he can use the man for his own purposes, the adversary of souls will let him reform as much as he pleases.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">45.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation.</sty>

[BODY] He takes another walk; he is so pleased with his elegant mansion that he calls upon other demons and invites them to his garnished home. The evil ones join him, and the inhabitants of the house are as eight to one of their former number. They “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">enter in and dwell there</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">:  </sty>they take the fullest

--- PAGE 193 ---

[BODY] possession and make a permanent stay. Their residence is secured beyond future likelihood of removal; and now the man is <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">worse than at the first;</sty> for the unclean spirits are more numerous and <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">more wicked.  </sty>The sinful man becomes more proud, and more unbelieving, or he becomes more vicious and more blasphemous than at the beginning. So much for a hopeful reformation, which indeed from the very first was hopeless, because Jesus was not there, and the Holy Spirit had no hand in it. Cunningly the unclean spirit submits to an apparent giving up of power that he may establish his dominion the more firmly. No doubt, relapses into sin are, like relapses in disease, even more dangerous than the original malady.

[BODY] In Christ’s day the Pharisees and others were in this case. The spirit which led the Jews to idolatry was gone, but the true God was not spiritually loved nor even known; and so the demon power held them still in possession. In the future, even in that <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">wicked generation,  </sty>in the form of hatred to Christ, and fanatical contempt of other nations, the evil spirit which had depraved Judaism, would yet display itself in a still more hideous shape; as it did from our Lord’s day and onward till the destruction of Jerusalem, when the race seemed to have gone fairly mad, under a diabolical influence which made them “hateful, and hating one another.” We may fear that our present age of “culture” and advancement will go onward till it reaches a similar goal. It is progressing towards infidelity, and advancing towards absurdity; while at the same time worldliness is rampant, and holiness is ridiculed.

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 12:46-50</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">OUR KING AND HIS EARTHLY RELATIVES</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">46.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">While he yet talked to the people, behold, his mother and brethren stood without, desiring to speak with him.</sty>

[BODY] The members of his family had come to take him, because they thought him beside himself. No doubt the Pharisees had so represented his ministry to his relatives that they thought they had better restrain him, lest he should procure his own destruction by his zealous preaching. Friends may be a good man’s greatest hindrance. They intruded upon his holy service “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">while he yet talked to the people.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>A mark of wonder is put before this record: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Behold.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>How dare they act in this manner? By the request of <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">his mother and his brethren  </sty>he is called away from the pressing engagement of teaching the people, which was his urgent lifework; but the call had no power over him. What ailed Mary that she joined in this transaction? Many a nervous mother has been ready to hold back her consecrated son when his courage has defied danger. Our Lord did not allow his love to his mother to turn him aside.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">47.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then one said unto him, Behold thy mother and thy brethren stand without desiring to speak with thee.</sty>

[BODY] An officious person reported the errand of the family: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">one said unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren stand without.  </sty>It<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>is hard when interruptions come from our own flesh and blood; for strangers are sure to back them up. Ignorantly or willfully, the reporting person lent himself to the design of the relatives by representing that they were <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">desiring to speak with him</sty>; though, indeed, they desired to take him. He who would not permit a disciple to neglect his duty on the plea of burying his father, how will he act now that his mother comes to hinder him? He will do the right thing. We may always find the rule of our conduct by asking the

--- PAGE 195 ---

[BODY] question, “What would Jesus do?”

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">48, 49.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  But he answered and said unto him that told him, Who is my mother? and who are my brethren? And he stretched forth his hand toward his disciples, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren!</sty>

[BODY] He does not reject the tender ties of his human nature, but he exhibits their true position as secondary to the spiritual bonds which united him to the spiritual family. Those who were related to him by the bonds of discipleship had in this the truest union with him. He pointed to “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">his disciples, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren!</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>All believers in Jesus are of the royal family, princes of the blood, brothers of the Christ. See how he owns the affinity, and bids all know it. “He is not ashamed to call them brethren.” In this instance his method of acknowledging them was singularly striking; he even set them before his earthly mother and brethren.

[BODY] Lord, let us know and enjoy our nearness to thyself. Help us also to care for thee as a mother for her son, and to love thee as a man should love his own brother.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">50.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.</sty>

[BODY] He enlarges upon the truth. Every doer of the Father’s will is thereby proved to be a true disciple, and he is to Jesus as near as a brother, as dear as a sister, as much cared for as mother. According to our condition and capacity, let us act towards our Lord the part of <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">brother  </sty>in help, of <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">sister</sty> in sympathy, of <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">mother  </sty>in tender love; for all these relationships act in both ways, and involve giving as well as<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>receiving. What a blessed “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">whosoever</sty>” is<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>this! It is not for ministers only, or for persons set apart to special service; but all who <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">do the Father’s will</sty> in any position of life are encompassed in the family circle of the Lord Christ.

[BODY] Our Lord Jesus had a little while before cut himself adrift from the bands of formality by routing the scribes and Pharisees, and now the knife goes

--- PAGE 196 ---

[BODY] deeper, and all that is of the flesh at its very best is divided from that which is of the spirit. Henceforth it is clear that after the flesh he knows no man any more; neither can we hope to know him by birth-right membership, or anything else that is of blood, or birth, or of the will of the flesh. The inner life which is akin to God, and shows itself in holiness, is that which gives us union with our Lord. Oh, to feel its influence more and more!

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 13:1-53</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">OUR KING SETS FORTH SEVEN PARABLES OF HIS KINGDOM</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">1.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1"> </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">THE same day went Jesus out of the house, and sat by the sea side.</sty>

[BODY] He was not afraid of being seized by his family, but freely went abroad. How serene was his behavior. On the beach, in the open air, he gave greater play to his imagination, and quitted the didactic style for the parabolical.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">2.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And great multitudes were gathered together unto him, so that be went into a ship, and eat; and the whole multitude stood on the shore.</sty>

The teacher <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">sat,</sty> and the people <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">stood:  </sty>we should have less sleeping in congregations if this arrangement still prevailed.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">3.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And he spake many things unto them in parables, saying, Behold, a sower went forth to sow.</sty>

[BODY] He had much instruction to give, and he chose to convey it <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">in parables.</sty> What wonderful pictures they were! for us, as well as for those who heard

[BODY] them! This parable of the sower is a mine of teaching concerning the kingdom; for the seed was “the word of the kingdom.” (See verse 19.)

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Behold!</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">:  </sty>every word is worthy of attention. [BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">4.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And when he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side and the fowls came and devoured them up.</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">When HE sowed, some seeds fell by the wayside:  </sty>even when the Chief Sower is at work, some seed fails. We know he sows the best of seed, and in the best manner; but some of it falls on the trodden path, and so lies uncovered and unaccepted of the soil. That soil was hard, and beaten down with traffic. There, too, on the wayside, we meet with dust to blind, settlements of mud to foul, and birds to pilfer: it is not a good place for good seed. No wonder, as the seeds lay all exposed, that <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the fowls came and devoured them up.  </sty>If truth does not enter the heart, evil influences soon remove it.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">5, 6.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Some fell upon stony place, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth: and when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away.</sty>

[BODY] Among the rocks, or on the shallow soil, with the unbroken rock-pan underneath, the seed fell; for if the sower had altogether avoided such places he might have missed some of the good ground. When the time came for the sun to put forth his force, the rootless plants instantly pined and died. “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">They had no deepness of earth,</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>and “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">no root</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">;  </sty>what could they do but <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">wither  </sty>quite <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">away</sty>? [BODY] the speedy growth met with speedy death. No trace remained.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">7.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them.</sty>

[BODY] The ground was originally a thornbrake, and had been cleared by <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the thorns  </sty>being cut down; but speedily the old roots sent out new shoots, and other weeds came up with them; and the tangled beds of thistles, thorns, nettles, and what not, strangled the feeble up-shootings of the wheat. The native plants <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">choked  </sty>the poor stranger. They would not permit the intrusive corn to share the field with them: evil claims a monopoly of our nature.

[BODY] Thus we have seen three sots of seed come to an untimely end.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">8.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold.</sty>

[BODY] This would repay all losses, especially at the highest rate of increase here quoted. To the bird, the weather, and the weeds, three sets of seeds have gone; yet, happily, one remains to increase and fill the barn. The sowing of good seed can never be a total failure: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">other fell into good ground</sty>.”

[BODY] The harvest was not equally great on every spot of fertile soil: it varied from an hundredfold to <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">thirtyfold.  </sty>All good ground is not alike good; and, besides, the situation may differ. Harvests are not all alike in the same farm, in the same season, and under same farmer; and yet each field may yield a fairly good harvest.

[BODY] Lord, if I cannot reach to a hundred fold, let me at least prove to be good ground by bearing thirtyfold.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">9.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">10. </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables?</sty>

[BODY] Perhaps the crowd had complained to the disciples that they could not see what their Master was driving at The apostles may have felt unable to reply. As the matter perplexed them, they did well to enquire of their infallible Teacher, rather than to invent an explanatory theory, which might have been altogether a mistake.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">11. </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven but to them it is not given.</sty>

[BODY] The usual reasons for the use of parable would be to make truth clear, to arrest attention, and to impress teaching upon the memory. But in this instance our Lord was, by his parabolic speech, fulfilling the judicial sentence which had been long before pronounced upon the apostate nation among whom he received such unworthy treatment. They were doomed to have the light and to remain willfully in the dark. To his own disciples our Lord would explain the parable, but not to the outside unbelieving throng. If any one among the multitude became sincerely anxious to know the Lord’s meaning, he would become his disciple, and then he would be taught “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">;  </sty>but those who rejected the Messiah would, while listening to parables, hear and not hear, see and not perceive.

[BODY] To hear the outward word is a common privilege: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">To know the mysteries</sty>” is<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>a gift of sovereign grace. Humbling truths. Salvation, and the knowledge by which it comes, are given as the Lord wills. There is such a thing as distinguishing grace after all; let the moderns revile the doctrine as they may.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">12.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">For whoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath.</sty>

[BODY] Those who had some understanding of spiritual truth would come to yet clearer light; but those who lived willfully in the dark, would, in the presence of light, become more and more bewildered, and would gain nothing but the discovery that they did not know what they thought they knew. An ignorant man going into a museum, or healing a learned lecture, only feels himself a greater fool. He learns nothing, because he is not able to comprehend the elementary terms of the science. It is just so with carnal men; spiritual truth rather blinds them than enlightens them.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">13.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, nether do they understand.</sty>

[BODY] This was his reason for <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">speaking to them in parables;  </sty>they could not understand spiritual things, and therefore he gave them no naked doctrine, for then they would not have listened at all. They did not really see what they saw, nor hear what they heard. The plainer the teaching, the more they were puzzled by it. They had become so morally and spiritually diseased. that the only thing they would notice was the attractive dress of a truth: for the truth itself they had no liking and no perception. To this day, marvels of creation, works of grace, deeds of providence, and ordinances of religion, are all as voiceless music, or painted suns, to carnal men: they hear not their teaching, they feel not their power.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">14.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive.</sty>

[BODY] That wonderful sixth chapter of Isaiah is constantly being quoted in the New Testament. How clearly it sets forth the doom of guilty Israel! Those who refuse to see are punished by becoming unable to see. The penalty of sin is to be left in sin. The Jews of our Lord’s day would trifle with what they heard, and so they were left to hear without understanding. Even the

--- PAGE 202 ---

[BODY] Messenger of the Covenant would speak in vain to them.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">15.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">For this people’s heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.</sty>

[BODY] They had deadened their own faculties. Perversity in sin had made them heartless, and deaf, and blind to all spiritual things. Thus, they blocked up the way of salvation against themselves, and used their utmost diligence to prevent their own conversion. It was but just that the truth should reach them in a manner which would condemn rather than convert. If it had come in any other form but the parabolic, they would not even have deigned to listen to it. In that form truth would have been more clearly seen than in any other if they had been willing to see it; but, as they were unwilling, the emblem became a dark lantern shutting the light from them. If men will willfully close their eyes, the very light shall blind them. Thus, when the Lord passes any by, it is due to their sin; but when he chooses any, it is not because they <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">are  </sty>better, but that he may make them better.

[BODY] This passage teaches that the possession of faculties is a small thing unless we fitly use them. Men should “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">see with their eyes, hear with their ears, and understand with their hearts.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>If they turn to Christ he will heal them, even of <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">gross  </sty>hearts, and <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">dull  </sty>ears, and <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">closed  </sty>eyes. But, alas! there is a generation which will not be <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">converted;  </sty>for they are proud of their blindness and grossness.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">16, 17.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear. [BODY] Happy men to be chosen to such a privilege! Grace has opened y our eyes and ears. <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Blessed are your eyes, for they see.  </sty>What wonders, treasures, revelations do they see! Eyes are blessed which gaze upon the mysteries

--- PAGE 203 ---

[BODY] of divine love. <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Blessed are your ears, for they hear;  </sty>hear something sweeter than the song of angels, even the voice of everlasting love from the heart of Jesus. Truly <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">to hear</sty> the gospel and <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">to see  </sty>its blessings is a high favor. [BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">18.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Hear ye therefore the parable of the sower.</sty>

[BODY] Because you see behind the curtain, and have grace given to discern the inner meaning through the outer metaphor, come and <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">hear  </sty>the explanation of <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the parable of the sower.</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">19.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the wicked one, and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart. [BODY] The gospel is “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the word of the kingdom</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">:  </sty>it has royal authority in it; it proclaims and reveals King Jesus, and it leads men to obedience to his sway. [BODY] Satan is always on the watch to hinder the Word: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Then cometh the wicked one</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>even at the moment when the seed fell. --- PAGE 204 ---

[BODY] highway, hard, and much frequented. The man was not an opposer, he “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">received seed</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">;  </sty>but he received the truth as he was, without the soil of his nature being changed; and the seed remained as it was, till the foul bird of hell took it off the place, and there was an end of it. [BODY] Lord, suffer none of us to be impervious to thy royal word; but whenever the smallest seed of truth falls on us, may we open our soul to it!

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">20, 21.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it; yet hath he not root in himself, but dureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by He is offended.</sty>

[BODY] Here the seed was the same and the sower the same, but the result somewhat different. In this case there was earth enough to cover the seed, and heat enough to make it grow quickly. May we all

--- PAGE 205 ---

[BODY] have broken hearts and prepared minds, that when truth comes to us it may take root in us and abide.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">22.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">He also that received seed among the thorn is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful.</sty>

[BODY] This class of hearers we know by personal acquaintance in this busy age. They <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">hear the word,  </sty>they are affected by the gospel, they take it as <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">seed</sty> into their minds, and it grows well for a season; but the heart cannot belong to two absorbing objects at the same time, and therefore these men cannot long yield themselves up to the world and Christ too. We cannot grow thorn and corn at the same time: the attempt is fatal to a harvest for Jesus.

[BODY] See how wealth is here associated with <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">care, deceitfulness,  </sty>and <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">unfruitfulness.  </sty>It is a thing to be handled with care. Why are men so eager to make their thorn-brake more dense with briars?

[BODY] Would not a good husbandman root out the thorns and brambles? Should we not, as much as possible, keep free from the care to get, to preserve, to increase, and to hoard worldly riches? Our heavenly Father will see that we have enough; why do we fret about earthly things? We cannot give our minds to these things and to the kingdom also.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">23.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But he that received seed into the good ground is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it; which also beareth fruit, and bringeth forth, some an hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.</sty>

[BODY] Here is the story of the Word’s success. This fourth piece of land will repay all charges. Of course, no one parable teaches all truth, and therefore we have no mention here of the ploughing which always precedes a fruitful harvest. No heart of man is good by nature: the good Lord had made this plot into “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">good ground.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>In this case, both thought and heart are engaged about the heavenly message, and the man “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">heareth the word and understandeth it.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>By<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>being understood lovingly, the truth gets into the man, and then it roots, it grows, it fruits, it rewards the sower. [BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">24.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field.</sty>

[BODY] Still to give us often the key-note of this gospel, our Lord speaks of “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the kingdom of heaven</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">;  </sty>and to continue his method of making truth so clear that only the willfully blind should fail to see it, he brings forth another plain and pregnant similitude. He is gone within his heavenly house, and has left his field to the care of his servants. Alas, that care is by no means what it should be!

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">25. </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.</sty>

[BODY] The servants are all too apt to sleep. There is a season when nature requires them to do so, and there are other times when sinful sloth persuades them to the same indulgence. Good, easy men, they cannot believe that anyone would do harm to their master’s field; besides,

--- PAGE 207 ---

[BODY] watching and driving away trespassers is unpleasant work. “Heresy-hunting” is the nickname for watchfulness. “Rigid Puritanism” is the contemptuous title for careful discipline. “Bigotry” is the title by which faithfulness is described. “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">While men slept</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>could any cultured person resist the spirit of the times, and keep awake?

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">His enemy came</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">:  </sty>we know who the enemy is. His time for work is in the night. He sleeps not when watchmen are steeped in slumber; but then is he specially active. Quietly, cunningly, without observation, that malicious one sowed the darnel, the bastard wheat; a something so like wheat that no one could tell the difference till they began to ripen. He brought in those who loved “modern thought”, and worldly amusements, who were by their talk Christian, and by their boasts profoundly spiritual; and having introduced them cunningly, he departed. He might have been suspected had he lingered upon the scene of his craft; and so he “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">went his way</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>to<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>do the like elsewhere. Satan is not omnipresent, but this he cunningly turns into an advantage, for he can often do more by his absence than by his presence. A known devil is only half a devil.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">26.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But when the blade was sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also.</sty>

[BODY] Good seed grows, and, alas! evil seed is equally full of the power to increase. Satan’s principles have a terrible vitality and rigor in them. [BODY] The darnel is up as soon as the wheat, and it looks so like it that it appears to be the selfsame thing. The field is ruined; its yield is poisoned by the mixture of a pernicious plant. What had the enemy gained for himself? Nothing: it was enough for him that he had injured the man he hated.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">27.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">So the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, didst not thou sow good seed in thy field? From whence then hath it tares?</sty>
