[BODY] Our great thought-rending King was not to be deceived either by their flattery or their crafty questioning: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">But Jesus perceived their wickedness;  </sty>for<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>it was that, with a vengeance. Malice and deceit designed

--- PAGE 385 ---

[BODY] his overthrow; but he saw through the cunning of his enemies, and perceived the wickedness that prompted them thus to assail him. Onlookers may not have perceived their wickedness, and our Lord’s disciples may have been puzzled as to how he would reply; but, as in all other trying circumstances, Jesus himself knew what he would do.

[BODY] Probably even his enemies did not expect such a question as he now put to them: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites?</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They hoped that they had disguised their real purpose so cleverly, that they must have been surprised to have the mask so quickly torn from their faces, and to be exposed to public gaze in their true character as “hypocrites.” Jesus compared them to stage-players, dissemblers, men acting a false part with intent to deceive. Rightly did he name them ; and wisely did he say to them, “Why tempt ye me? “It is as if he had said, “You see that I am not deceived by your false and flattering speeches, I can read the malice that is written in a our hearts, you are just powerless before me if I choose to treat you as I can do; what can poor, puny creatures, such as ye are, do against me? Why <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">tempt  </sty>ye me? “There is infinite scorn in our Savior’s question; yet there is an undertone of pity even for those who deserved it not: “Why tempt ye me? Have I given you any cause why you should seek to entrap me? Why are, you so foolish as to ask questions which must be to your own hurt?”

[BODY] Whenever men pretend great reverence for Jesus, and then seek, by their erroneous teaching, or their science falsely so-called, to overthrow his gospel, they are base hypocrites.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">19.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Shew me the tribute money. And they brought unto him a penny.</sty>

[BODY] Having exposed their folly and hypocrisy, Jesus proceeds to put them publicly to shame. He said to them, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Shew me the tribute money.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>This request on his part, and their compliance with it, would make the whole matter more vivid and impressive to the bystanders. When there is something to see and handle, a lesson becomes the more striking. Our Lord asked them to show him a specimen of the coin usually paid for the capitation tax: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">and they brought unto him a penny,  </sty>a<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  denarius.  </sty>This

--- PAGE 386 ---

[BODY] coin represented the daily pay of a Roman soldier, and in the parable of the vineyard it was said to be the daily wage of the laborer. Had these men guessed the use to which Jesus would put the denarius, they would not have so quickly procured one for him. They bought their own confusion with that coin. They would never afterwards be able to look upon the tribute money without remembering how they were foiled in their attempt to entangle the hated Nazarene.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">20, 21.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription? They say unto him, Caesar’s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s.</sty>

[BODY] He asked another question, that they might themselves assist in replying to themselves: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">He saith unto them,  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Whose is this image and superscription</sty>? “Or rather, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">inscription.  </sty>Before them were the image and inscription of the Roman emperor on the piece of money; but he would make them say as much, so he asks, “Whose is this?” The Jewish Rabbis taught that “if a king’s coin is current in a country, the men of the country do thereby evidence that they acknowledge him for their lord.”

[BODY] When we are dealing with ungodly men, it is well if we can make them to be their own accusers.

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">They say unto him,  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Caesar’s</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>No other answer was possible. This tribute money was not a shekel of Jewish coinage, but money of the Roman empire. This was a plain proof that, whether they liked it or not, they were Roman subjects, and Caesar was their ruler. What then must follow but that they should pay to their acknowledged ruler his due? <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Then saith he unto them,  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar’s.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Whatever belongs to Caesar is to be rendered, to him. Jesus did not say what was Caesar’s, the coin itself settled the question of paying tribute; his reply covered all the duties of loyal subjects to the ruler under whose jurisdiction they lived; but this did not touch the sovereignty of God. Jehovah held rule over consciences and hearts; and they must see to it that, as Caesar had his own, the Lord had his own also. Render therefore “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">unto God the things that are God’s.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>This was not an

--- PAGE 387 ---

[BODY] evasive reply on Christ’s part; it was full of meaning, and very much to the point; and yet it was so put that neither Pharisees nor Herodians could make anything out of it for party purposes, or for their wretched design of entangling Jesus in his talk. Neither of the two sects turned a penny by their penny.

[BODY] To us the lesson of this incident is, that the State has its sphere, and we must discharge our duties to it; but we must not forget that God has his throne, and we must not allow the earth-kingdom to make us traitors to the heaven-kingdom. Caesar must keep, his place and by no means go beyond it; but God must have the spiritual dominion to himself alone.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">22.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">When they had heard these words, they marveled, and left him, and went their way.</sty>

[BODY] They had some sense left even if they had no feeling. They saw that their plot had ignominiously failed; <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">they marveled  </sty>at the wisdom with which Christ had baffled their cunning; the, knew that it was hopeless to continue the conflict: so they <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">left him, and went their way</sty>. Their way was not his way. They had already admitted, in their a flattering speech, that he was a true teacher of God’s way; and now they. completed their own condemnation by leaving him, and going their own way.

[BODY] Lord, save us from following their evil example! Rather, may we cleave to Christ, and go his way!

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 22:23-33</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE KING AND THE SADDUCEES</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">23.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">The same day came to him the Sadducees, which say that there is no resurrection, and asked him,</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">The same day:  </sty>there was no rest for Jesus; as soon as one set of enemies was driven away, another company marched up to attack him. He had silenced the Pharisees and the Herodians; now <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">there came to him the Sadducees,  </sty>the<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>broad churchmen, the rationalists of our Savior’s day: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">which say that there is no resurrection.  </sty>They rejected a great deal more of the teaching of the Scriptures than this one point of the resurrection; but this is specially mentioned here as it was the subject on which they hoped to entrap or confuse the Savior. The Sadducees “say that there is no resurrection”; yet they came to Christ to ask what would happen, in a certain contingency, “in the resurrection.” They evidently thought that they could state a case which would bring into contempt the doctrine of the resurrection of the dead. They might have taken warning from the experience of the Pharisees and the Herodians; but doubtless they felt so sure of their own position that they expected to succeed though the others had so conspicuously failed.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">24.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Saying, Master, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise Up seed unto his brother</sty>

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Master;</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>they came with affected respect for the great “Teacher.” They were as polite as the previous company of assailants; but, like them, though the words of their mouth were smoother than butter, war was in their heart: though their words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords (Psalm 55:21).

--- PAGE 389 ---

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Moses said</sty>”: they gave the substance, though not the exact words recorded in Deuteronomy 25:5. The law of Moses, in this as in many other shatters, recognized existing customs, and imposed certain regulations upon them. For a man<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>to die without leaving a child to bear his name, and enter upon his inheritance, was regarded as so great a calamity that the Jews judged that every possible means must be taken to prevent it. The practice here described prevails among various Oriental nations even to this day.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">25-28.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Now there were with us seven brethren: and the first, when he had married a wife, deceased and, having no issue, left his wife unto his brother: likewise the second also, and the third, unto the seventh. And last of all the woman died also. Therefore in the resurrection whose wife shall she be of the seven if or they all had her.</sty>

[BODY] These Sadducees may have known such a case as they stated, though it is extremely unlikely; more probably, this was one of the stock stories they were in the habit of telling in order to cast ridicule upon the resurrection. They had no belief in spiritual beings; therefore, they supposed that, if there were a future state, it would be similar to the present. Having stated their case, they put to the Savior this perplexing question: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">In the resurrection whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They doubtless thought that this question would puzzle Christ, as it had puzzled others to whom it had been put; but he had no more difficulty in answering this than he had with the previous enquiries.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">29.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Jesus answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Jesus answered and said unto them,  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Ye do err:</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>the error was not with him, but with them. Their supposed argument was based on their own erroneous notions about the unseen world; and when the light of God’s Word was poured upon their seven men of straw, they vanished into thin air. The answer to objectors, skeptics, infidels today, may be given in our Lord’s words: “Ye do err, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>These Sadducees thought that they had found a

--- PAGE 390 ---

[BODY] difficulty in the Scriptures; but their error arose from their “not knowing the Scriptures.” This is the root of almost all error, ignorance of the Inspired Word of God. These men were acquainted with the letter, but they did not really know the Scriptures, or they would have found there abundant revelations concerning the resurrection.

[BODY] Their error arose, also, from ignorance of “the power of God.” The resurrection of the dead is one of the greatest proofs of the power of God, with whom all things are possible. These Sadducees limited the Holy One of Israel in their ignorance or denial of his power. What is there about the resurrection that is incredible to the man who knows “the power of God”? Surely, he, who created all things by the word of his power, can, by that same power, raise the dead in his own appointed time.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">30.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.</sty>

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">In the resurrection</sty>” our Lord implied that there is a resurrection; he did not even stay to prove that truth, but went on to speak of the resurrection life as being of a higher order<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  than our  </sty>present natural life: “they<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in hearer.</sty>” Our Savior’s answer struck at another Sadducean error; his questioners did not believe in angels. Jesus did not attempt to prove the existence of angels; but took that fact also for granted, by saying that, “in the resurrection “men” are as the angels of God in heaven.” He did not say that they are changed into angels; but, as Luke records his words, “they are equal unto the angels.” They are spiritual beings, as Paul explains in 1 Corinthians 15.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">31, 32.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken unto you by God, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.</sty>

[BODY] Our Savior now gives these Sadducees further instruction “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">as touching the resurrection of the dead.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>He used the formula he so often employed in speaking to those who professed to read the Scriptures:

--- PAGE 391 ---

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Have ye not read?</sty>” You reject the oral traditions which the Pharisees accept and teach in place of the commandments of God, have you not read <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">that which was spoken unto you by God?</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Jesus always manifested the utmost reverence for the revealed Word of God. He here showed that the truth made known in the Scriptures is a very personal matter This message was spoken unto these Sadducees, although they knew it not; it was spoken by God, yet they received it not.

[BODY] How necessary it is that we should search the scriptures, lest there should be divinely-revealed truths that so have not even read! How needful, also, is the teaching of the Holy Spirit, lest we should read, as these Sadducees did, and yet not know the Scriptures!

[BODY] Jesus might have referred to many passages in the Old Testament about the resurrection; but as the Sadducees regarded the Pentateuch with special honor, he quoted what Moses had recorded in Exodus 3:6<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">:  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob;</sty>” and then added his own comment and exposition: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob had long been dead when the Lord spoke to Moses out of the burning bush. His words implied that the patriarchs were still living. His covenant was made with those who still existed.

[BODY] There is much teaching in this truth, that “God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.” Some suppose that, until the resurrection, the saints are virtually non-existent; but this cannot a be. Though disembodied, they still live; Jesus does not argue about it, but he states the fact as beyond all question. The living God is the God of diving men; and Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are still alive, and identified as the same persons who lived on the earth. God is the God of Abraham’s body as well as of his soul, for the covenant seal was set upon his flesh. The grave cannot hold any portion of the covenanted ones; God is the God of our entire being, spirit, soul, and body.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">33.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And when the multitude heard this, they were astonished at his doctrine.</sty>

--- PAGE 392 ---

[BODY] Our Lord’s reply to the Sadducees was so complete that they were “put to silence” (v. 34). They did not attempt any further assault upon him, for they must have been convinced of their own impotence. Those who had stood by as listeners, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the multitude,  </sty>that had gathered as crowds delight to do when there is a public discussion, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">were astonished at his doctrine.</sty> They were “astonished” both at the matter and the manner of Christ’s teaching. This is an expression that we often find in the life of our Lord; but apparently those who were “astonished” did not accept his teaching. They talked to one another about the marvelous way<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>in which he answered all questions; but they did not admit that such a Teacher could be none other than the long looked-for Messiah. Even the scribes, who complimented Christ upon his answer (Luke 20:39), saying, “Master, thou hast well said,” did not follow up that confession by becoming his disciples.

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 22:34-40</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE KING TESTED BY A LAWYER</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">34.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But when the Pharisees had heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, they were gathered together.</sty>

[BODY] The multitude that had listened to Christ, and had been “astonished” at his answers to the Sadducees, would soon publish the tidings of their defeat <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">When the Pharisees had heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence,  </sty>they doubtless felt pleased that their natural enemies had been routed, but grieved that Jesus had again proved victorious in argument. He had, in one day, baffled the chief priests and elders of the people, Pharisees and their disciples, Herodians and Sadducees. If he continued to prevail, all the people would be won over to his side. So once more they met in consultation: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">they were gathered together</sty>. They must think of some fresh device, some new plan for his overthrow. How persevering wicked men are in their evil courses! While we deplore their wickedness, let us imitate their persistency.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">35.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">The one of them, which was a lawyer asked him a question, tempting him, and saying,</sty>

[BODY] Apparently, the result of their conference was that they selected one of their number to put to Jesus another enquiry: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">one of them, which was a lawyer, asked him a question.  </sty>Mark says that this man was one of the scribes, one of those constantly engaged in copying the Law, and also one who explained its meaning to the people. He was a gentleman “learned in the Law.” He came, either as the representative of the Pharisees, or on his own account, and asked Jesus a question, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">tempting him</sty>. Putting the mildest meaning on the word “tempting”, it conveys the idea of testing and trying in an unfriendly sense. Probably he was a man of clearer light and greater discernment than his associates; for he was evidently only

--- PAGE 394 ---

[BODY] half-hearted in the work of “tempting” Christ. Mark says that he had heard our Lord’s words to the Sadducees, “and perceiving that he had answered them well,” he put his own question to Jesus. He was evidently a man of candor, possessing a considerable amount of spiritual knowledge. This may help to explain the reason for his question:—

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">36.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Master, which is the great commandment in the law?</sty>

[BODY] According to the Rabbis, there were many commandments which were secondary, and others which were of the first importance. They often put commands, which really were comparatively small, on a par with those which were<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>greatest. One of them even ventured to say that the commands of the Rabbis were more important than the commands of the Law, because the commands of the Law were little and great, but all the commands of the Rabbis were great. Some of them regarded eating with unwashen hands as being as great a crime as murder; and they would classify the rubbing of ears of corn together on the Sabbath-day with adultery; so that they caused great confusion as to the real order of moral precepts. It was, therefore, most desirable to get from this wise Teacher, whom the scribe addressed as “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Master</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>an<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>authoritative answer to the question, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Which is the great commandment in the law?  </sty>“The enquiry was one which would be sure to entangle the Savior if he did not answer it wisely; and therein the lawyer tempted, tested, tried, and proved him.

[BODY] Blessed be his dear name, he can stand any test to which he may be put! Satan tempted, tested, and tried him to the uttermost of his power; but even he never found any flaw, or fault, or failing in him.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">37, 38.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Jesus said unto him. Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment.</sty>

[BODY] These were very familiar words to our Lord’s hearers, for all devout Jews were in the habit of repeating them every morning and evening. Deuteronomy 6:4-9, from which our Savior quoted, was one of the four passages which were worn as “phylacteries” (23:5). <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Jesus, said unto him,</sty> “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Because he is

--- PAGE 395 ---

[BODY] our God, Jehovah claims our heart’s love. As our Creator, Preserver, Provider, and Judge, he commands us to yield to him all our heart’s affection; to love him first, best, heartiest; out of all comparison to the love we have to any fellow-creature, or to ourselves.

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">And with all thy soul.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>We are<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>to love God with all our life, to love him more than our life; so that, if necessary, we would give up our life rather than give up our love to God.

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">And with all thy mind.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>We are to love God with our intellect, with all the powers of our mind, bringing memory, thought, imagination, reason, judgment, and all our mental powers, as willing subjects to bow at God’s feet in adoration and love.

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">This is the first and great commandment.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>It is “first” in point of time, for it was binding upon the angels before man was created; it was binding upon Adam from the hour of his creation in the image of God. It is “first” in importance, for there is no love to a creature worthy of comparison with love to the Creator. This commandment is also “great”, because it comprehends all others, and because its demands are so great, namely, the whole love of our heart, and soul, and mind.

[BODY] Who can render to God this perfect love? None of our fallen race. Salvation by the words of the Law is clearly an impossibility, for we cannot obey even the first commandment. There is<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>One who has obeyed it, and the obedience of Christ is reckoned as, the obedience of all who trust him. Being free from legal condemnation, they seek ever after to obey this “great and first commandment” (R.V.) by the power of the Holy! Spirit, who dwells within them.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">39.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And the second is like unto it, Thou shall love thy a neighbor as thyself.</sty>

[BODY] The answer is wider than the question. The lawyer asked about “the great commandment”; Christ answered his enquiry, and then added, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">and the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Who of us has really loved his neighbor as himself? Under the Gospel this

--- PAGE 396 ---

[BODY] commandment is certainly not less binding than under

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">40.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.</sty>

[BODY] The teaching of Moses and all the prophets might be summarized in “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">these two commandments.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>The duty<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>of loving God and loving our neighbor as we love ourselves is the supreme subject of the divine revelation. On this, as on a great peg, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">hang all the law and the prophets.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Remove the peg, and what have you left as a support for the teaching given by the Lord through the holy men of old who wrote as they were moved by the Holy Ghost?

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 22:41-46</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE KING ASKING QUESTIONS</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">41, 42.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them, saying, What think ye of Christ? whose son is he? They say unto him, The son of David.</sty>

[BODY] ‘The King now carried the war into the enemy’s country. He had answered all the questions put to him; it was his turn to propound some to those who had come to examine him. <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">While the Pharisees were gathered together,  </sty>that is, while they still lingered near him, disappointed and defeated, yet watching for any opportunity of assailing him, Jesus <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">asked them, saying,  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">What think ye of Christ,</sty>” “Our Lord here sets his servants the example of how they should deal with cavilers, quibblers, objectors. Having wisely answered all their questions, he pressed home upon them the question of questions: “What think ye of Christ?” They had tried to puzzle him with their enquiries about Church and State, the future life, and the relative value of the commandments; but he put to them the much more vital question, “What think ye of Christ?”

[BODY] Jesus also pressed upon his hearers further enquiry about “the Christ” (R. V.), for the words used evidently mean the Messiah: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Whose son is he?</sty>” <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">They say unto him  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">The son of David.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They knew that the promised Deliverer would be descended from David; but they either did not know, or would not confess, that he had a divine as well as a human origin. This the Savior brings out by further questions.

--- PAGE 398 ---


[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">43-45.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  He saith unto them, How them doth David in spirit call him Lord, saying, The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool? If David then call him Lord, how is he his son?</sty>

[BODY] These questions of our Lord themselves contain the answers to the present-day critics who deny the divine inspiration of the Scriptures, and the Davidic authorship and Messianic application of certain Psalms. <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">He saith unto them,  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">How then doth David in spirit call him Lord?</sty>” quoting from Psalm 110:1, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">saying, The LORD said unto My Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool,</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>our Savior declared that these were the words of David, speaking “by the Holy Ghost” (see Mark 12:36), concerning the Christ, the Messiah. This ought for ever to settle the question about the inspiration, authorship, and application of that Psalm at least. “The LORD said unto my Lord,” — Jehovah said unto my Adonai: David, by the Holy Ghost; learned what the Father said unto the Son; and thus he was brought into connection with the whole sacred Trinity. “Sit thou on my right hand”: the Messiah was bidden to rest after his great mediatorial work was accomplished, and to sit on his Father’s right hand, in the place of honor, power, and majesty. “Till I make thine enemies thy footstool”: Jesus is to keep his seat till his foes are all prostrate at his feet.

[BODY] This was the problem the Pharisees had to solve: if the Messiah was David’s Son, how was it that David, by the Holy Ghost, called him his Lord? The Christ must be something more than mere man; otherwise the Psalmist’s words would have been unsuitable, and even blasphemous. He was higher than the angels, for unto none of them did Jehovah ever stay, “Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool “(Hebrews 1:13).

--- PAGE 399 ---

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">46.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And no man was able to answer him a word, neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any more questions. If the Pharisees could have denied that the Psalm had reference to the Messiah</sty>, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">it would have been easy for them to reply to Christ</sty>’<sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">s question</sty>; <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">but no man was able to answer him a word. The Rabbis of our Savior</sty>’<sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">s day admitted that this was one of the Messianic Psalms</sty>, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">without recognizing what their admission involved</sty>; <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">in later times</sty>, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">as at the present day</sty>, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">false teachers sought to wrest it from its proper meaning</sty>.

[BODY] Christ’s questions silenced his adversaries in a double sense; first, they could not answer him a word; and next, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any  </sty>He remained Master of the field. They could not entrap or entangle him in his talk; if they would put him to silence, they must do it by putting him to death.

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 23:1-12</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE KING’S WARNING AGAINST FALSE TEACHERS</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">1.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1"> </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">THEN spake Jesus to the multitude, and to his disciples, saying, The sribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat: all therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Then spake Jesus to the multitude:  </sty>the<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>King commenced his final address to the people. He was soon to withdraw himself from them; but first he would put them on their guard against their false teachers. They had heard what he had said to the scribes and Pharisees; now they would hear what he said <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">of</sty> them. <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">And to his disciples:  </sty>according to Luke, Jesus spoke to his disciples “in the audience of all the people.” His theme was one that concerned the whole population as well as his own disciples. He knew that he would shortly be taken away from them; therefore he warned them against those who would seek their ruin: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat: all therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>It<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>was the duty of Moses to expound to the people the Law of God. The scribes and Pharisees occupied his place; but alas! the Spirit that guided him was not in them. They spoke as from the chair of Moses, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">ex cathedra, as  </sty>we say; and as far as they really filled his seat, and followed his sayings, their words were to be obeyed. Our Savior could not have intended the people to heed their false comments and foolish glosses upon the Law of Moses; for he had already declared that by their traditions they had transgressed the commandment of God, and made it of none effect.

[BODY] At this time, however, our Lord was speaking of another grievous fault in the scribes and Pharisees; namely, that they said one thing and did another: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">But do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Sad indeed is the state of that religious teacher of whom the Searcher of hearts has to say, “Do as he says<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>and not as he does.” Many such are with us still, preaching one thing, and practicing another. May the Lord preserve

--- PAGE 401 ---

[BODY] the people from following their evil example!

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">4.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.</sty>

[BODY] The contrast between the true Teacher and the false ones is clearly brought out by this verse: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">They bind heavy burdens to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Their regulations as to moral and ceremonial observances were like huge faggots or crushing burdens bound together, and made into a weight intolerable for any man to carry. Many of these rules by themselves were grievous enough; but all together they formed a yoke that neither the people nor their fathers could bear. The scribes and Pharisees piled the great load upon them; but neither helped them; to sustain it, nor offered to relieve them of any portion of it: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>How different was Christ’s teaching: “Come unto me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest!” Taking their burdens of sin and sorrow and care upon his own shoulders, he exchanges them for his easy yoke, which itself gives rest to all who wear it.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">5-7.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments, and love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogue, and greetings in the markets, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi.</sty>

[BODY] This was the fatal flaw in their character: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">But all their works they do for to be seen of men.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>So<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>long as they stood well in the sight of their fellow-creatures, they cared little or nothing how they appeared to the eye of God. They were very particular about the literal observance of certain Mosaic injunctions, although they completely missed the spiritual meaning of them: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">They make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Four passages from the Law<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>Exodus 3:3-10, 11-16; Deuteronomy 6:4-9, 11:13-21, were written on strips of parchment, and worn on the forehead and the hand or arm as amulets, or preservatives. These the scribes and Pharisees made especially prominent,

--- PAGE 402 ---

[BODY] yet all the while the Word of the Lord was not hidden in their hearts, nor obeyed in their lives. The Lord commanded the children of Israel to make fringes in the borders of their garments, and upon the fringe a ribband or thread of blue, that they might look upon it, and remember all the commandments of the Lord, and do them (Numbers 15:38, 39). These ritualists of our Savior’s day were very scrupulous about having deep fringes or large tassels to their garments; but they remembered not the commandments of tlle Lord to do them. Many keep the laws of God to the eye, but violate them in the heart From such deceit may the Spirit of truth preserve us!

[BODY] Jesus next put together four things that the scribes and Pharisees loved: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Whether they met with their fellow-men for feasting, for worship, for business, or for instruction, they loved to be first and foremost. This is a common sin, and one into which we may easily fall. Our Lord felt it necessary to warn even his disciples against that evil, for his next words were evidently spoken specially to them.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">8-10.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Christ; and all ye are brethren. [BODY] In the Church of Christ, all titles and honors which exalt men and give occasion for pride are here forbidden. In the Christian commonwealth we should seek to realize a truer “Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity,” than that for which the world clamors in vain. He who is called “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Rabbi</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>robs Christ of his honor as the only Master or Teacher of his disciples: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">for one is your Master, even, Christ.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>He<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>also takes from his fellow-Christians the privilege that they share equally with him<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">:  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">and all ye are brethren.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Those who use such titles as “Holy Father “and “Right Reverend Father in God “would have a difficulty in explaining any our Savior’s words: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Call, no man your father upon the earth: for one is your Father, which is in heaven.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>In the tenth verse, our Lord’s words might be rendered: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Neither be ye called leaders (guides, instructors):</sty>

--- PAGE 403 ---

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">for one is your Leader (Guide, Instructor), even the Christ (the Messiah).</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>If<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>we follow him, we cannot go wrong.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">11, 12.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant. And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.</sty>

[BODY] This is nearly the same lesson that is recorded in chapter 20., verse 27. Our Lord had to repeat many times this law of his kingdom: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">He that is greatest among you shall be your servant.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>You are all equal; but if there is one amongst you who claims to be the greatest, he shall be the servant of all. Where our King rules, any one of his disciples who exalts himself shall be abased; while, on the other hand, the one who humbles himself shall be exalted. The way to rise is to sink self; the lower we fall in our own esteem, the higher shall we rise in our Master’s estimation.

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 23:13-33</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE KING PRONOUNCING WOES</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">13. </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.</sty>

[BODY] While our Savior was speaking to the people and his disciples, the scribes and Pharisees may have again drawn near. At any rate, his next words were addressed to them: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees</sty>, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">hypocrites!</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>This is the first of eight “woes”, in which the Lord Jesus both foretells the doom of the hypocrites gathered before him, and reveals the depth of his pity even for them. In seven of the eight “woes” he calls them “hypocrites”, in one he addresses them as “blind guides.” This first “woe” was pronounced against them because, as far as they could, they “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">shut up the kingdom of heaven against men.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>This was a terrible charge to be brought against them by him who could read their hearts, and who could truthfully say to them, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in</sty>.” They ought to have helped men into the kingdom; instead of doing so, they hindered those who were entering. Are there not false teachers, nowadays, who put stumbling-stones instead of stepping-stones in the way of those who are entering the kingdom of heaven?

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">14.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour windows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.</sty>

[BODY] The second “woe” was supported by two most serious accusations, which our Lord would not have uttered if they had not been true: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">ye devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayer.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Either of these sins by itself would have been very grievous; the two together were sufficient to sink those who were guilty of them to the lowest hell. The men who had defrauded widows would have to answer for their misdeeds

--- PAGE 405 ---

[BODY] to the widows’ “Judge “(Psalm 68:5). Those who had sought to cover their crimes with the<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>cloak of superior sanctity deserved to be stripped before the people they had deceived, and to hear the King’s righteous sentence: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>These words prove that there are degrees of punishment, as there are gradations in glory. All the ungodly will be judged and condemned by the Righteous Judge, but “the greater condemnation” will be reserved for the hypocrites who have “for a pretense” made “long prayers” while, behind the mask, they have been devouring the property of widows and the fatherless.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">15.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.</sty>

[BODY] The third “woe” related to the unholy zeal of the scribes and Pharisees in gaining adherents to Judaism and their own party, and by the process making them even worse than themselves. They freely gave time and trouble to the work with<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>the prospect of a very slight return: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They would, as it were, drag the Great Sea with a seine net in the hope of entangling one proselyte in its meshes; or they would go over all the land in order to persuade one Gentile to be circumcised so as to become “a Jew outwardly.” The result to the proselyte was only evil: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">When he is made, ye make him two fold: more the child of hell than yourselves.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Perverts usually become bigots. The proselyte would naturally imitate the vices of his hypocritical teachers, without having that knowledge of the Scriptures which might to some extent exercise a wholesome restraint upon them. The circumcised heathen would be a Judas rather than a Jew, a veritable “son of perdition.”

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">16-19.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Woe unto you, ye blind guides, which say, whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifieth the gold? [BODY] The form of the fourth “woe” differs from all the rest; in the other seven, our Savior said, “Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! “In this case, his words were<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Woe unto you, ye blind guides!</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They were nominally the religious guides of the Jews; but they were really “blind guides.” Sin, prejudice, bigotry, and hypocrisy had blinded their eyes. This was the case with the scribes and Pharisees; they were willfully foolish and willingly blind.

[BODY] Our Lord here condemned their misleading teaching concerning oaths. They actually taught that, if a man swore<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">by the temple</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">, his  </sty>oath was not binding; but that, if he swore “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">by the gold of the temple</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>he was bound by his oath; and, in like manner, they declared that an oath “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">by the altar</sty>” was not binding; but that, if a man <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">swore  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">by the gift that is upon the altar</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>he was<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>bound by his oath! [BODY] Jesus had forbidden all swearing (chapter 5., verses 34-36); so that he was not exalting one form of oath over another, but rather pointing out the folly and blindness of the scribes and Pharisees in reversing the right order of things. If any swearing, had been permissible, an oath “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">by the temple</sty>” must have been more binding than one “by the gold of the temple” yet

--- PAGE 407 ---

[BODY] these false teachers said, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">It is nothing.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>When men once quit the plain teaching of Christ, it is easy for them to go into all manner of heresies and absurdities.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">20-22.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Whoso therefore shall swear by the altar, sweareth by it, and by all things thereon. [BODY] The Jews invented fantastic forms of swearing in order to evade the use of the divine name. Our Lord therefore next proved the utter failure of all their attempts. Swearing “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">by the altar</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>was swearing “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">by all things thereon.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>An oath “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">by the temple</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>was really “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">by him that dwelleth therein</sty>.” The binding force of the oath could not lie in the mere building; but in the most High God, who condescended to dwell therein. Many Jews would swear “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">by hea</sty>v<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">en</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>although they would not call God to be a witness to their adjuration; but Jesus showed that they were doing the very thing they tried to avoid: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">He that shall swear by heaven, sweareth by the throne of God, and by him that sitteth thereon.</sty>” The only right course for us is to obey our Lord’s command, “I say unto you, swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God’s throne: nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.”

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">23, 24.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cumin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat and swallow a camel.</sty>

[BODY] In this fifth “woe” our Lord called the scribes and Pharisees both “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">hypocrites  </sty>“and “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">blind: guides.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They were “hypocrites” as to their own character and conduct, and “blind guides” as the religious leaders of the nation. Jesus first spoke of their scrupulous attention to certain minor

--- PAGE 408 ---

[BODY] matters: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Ye pay tithe of of mint and anise and cummin.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Some of them were so punctilious about paying tithes that they even gave to the temple service the tenth of the herbs they bought in the market, as well as of those they grew in their gardens. Although they were so particular about things that were of secondary importance, they “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">omitted the weightier, matters of the law, judgment (or, justice) mercy, and faith</sty>.” Their hearts were not right in the sight of God, therefore their minds were unbalanced; they counted the lesser requirements of the Law as of the first importance, while they “omitted the weightier matters” altogether. Our Lord did not blame them for paying the tithes; but he showed that they ought first to have exercised “justice, mercy and faith”: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>No commandment of God is non-essential; but that which relates to the condition of the heart and the life in the sight of the Lord Jehovah must receive our first and best attention.

[BODY] Jesus used a very expressive simile to set forth the inconsistency of the scribes and Pharisees: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Ye blind guides, which strain at (or, out) a gnat, and swallow a camel.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They rewarded trifles as if they were of first importance, and so, as it were, strained out gnats from their wine, lest they should be choked; but they committed great sins<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>without any compunctions of conscience, and thus, in effect, swallowed a camel, an unclean animal, equal in size to an almost innumerable quantity of gnats. There are gnat-strainers among us still, who apparently have no difficulty in swallowing a camel, “hump and all.”

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE KING’S FAREWELL TO HIS CAPITAL</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">34-36.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city: that upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar. [BODY] Our great King knew that his earthly life was soon to end; he was, in fact, about to utter his final farewell to the people gathered in the tenmple. But, before leaving them, he delivered a royal and prophetical message: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>None but the King of kings could speak thus without blasphemy. He foretold what kind of reception his servants would have from the Jews: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">And some of then ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them I shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute thein from city to city.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>All this was literally fufilled.

[BODY] The object of the King in sending his last representatives was that the guilty city should be left for ever without excuse when its measure of iniquity should be full, and its awful doom be sealed. “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed? upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>The destruction of Jerusalem was more terrible than anything that the world has ever witnessed, either before or since. --- PAGE 413 ---

[BODY] slain in Jerusalem was amply avenged when the whole city became veritable Aceldama, or field of blood.

[BODY] The Kingly Prophet foretold the time of the end: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>It was before that generation had passed away that Jerusalem was besieged and destroyed. There was a sufficient interval for the full proclamation of the gospel by the apostles and evangelists of the early Christian Church, and for the gathering out of those who recognized the crucified Christ as their true Messiah. Then came the awful end, which the Savior foresaw and foretold, and the prospect of which wrung from his lips ancl heart the sorrowful lament that followed his prophecy of the doom awaiting his guilty capital.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">37.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!</sty>

[BODY] What a picture of pity and disappointed love the King’s face must have presented when, with flowing tears, he uttered these words! [BODY] the Jews was left desolate when Jesus departed from them; and the temple,the holy and beautiful “house”, became a spiritual desolation when Christ finally left it. Jerusalem was too far gone to be rescued from its self-sought doom.

[BODY] Amid all this gloom there was one gleam of light: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that comethin the name of the Lord.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>After his death and resurrection, the Lord Jesus, appeared many times to his disciples, but not once to the unbelieving Jews. The signs of the times all tell us that his coming draweth nigh. Oh, that Christians and Jews alike were on the look-out for the true Messiah, whose message to all is, “Behold, I am coming quickly!”

[BODY] It must have been a peculiarly trying time for the women who had to flee from their homes just when they needed quiet and rest. How thoughtful and tender was our pitiful Savior in thus sympathizing with suffering mothers in their hour of need! “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Flight… in the winter</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>or<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">on the sabbath day</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>would have been attended with special difficulties; so the disciples were exhorted to “pray” that some other time might be available. The Lord knew exactly when they would be able to escape, yet he bade them pray that their flight might not be in the winter, nor on the Sabbath-day. the wise men of the present day would have said that prayer was useless under such conditions; not so the great Teacher and Example of his praying people; he taught that such a season was the very time for special supplication.

[BODY] The reason for this injunction was thus stated by the <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Savior:  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">For there shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Read the record written by Josephus of the destruction of Jerusalem, and see how truly our Lord’s words were fulfilled. The Jews impiously said, concerning the death of Christ, “His blood be on us, and on our children.” Never did any other people invoke such an awlful curse upon themselves, and upon no other nation did such a judgment ever fall. We read of Jews crucified till there was no more wood for making crosses; of thousands of the people slaying one another in their fierce faction fights within the city; of so many of them being sold for slaves that they became a drug in the market, and all but valueless; and of the fearful carnage when the Romans at length entered the doomed capital; and the blood-curdling story exactly bears out the Savior’s statement uttered nearly forty years before the terrible events occurred.

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE KING SPEAKS OF THE TIME OF HIS COMING</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">32-33.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh: so likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors. [BODY] Our Lord here evidently returns to often made use of its illuminated the subject of the destruction of Jerusalem, and in these words gives his apostles warning concerning the signs of the times. He had recently used the barren fig tree as an object-lesson; he now bids his disciples “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">learn a parable of the fig tree</sty>” and all the trees (Luke 21:31). God’s great book of nature is full of illustrations for those who have eyes to perceive them; and the Lord Jesus, the great Creator, often made use of its illuminated pages in conveying instruction to the minds of his hearers. On this occasion, he used a simple simile from the parable of the fig-tree: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They could not mistake so plain a token of the near return of summer; and Jesus would have them read quite as quickly the signs that were to herald the coming judgment on Jerusalem: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>The Revised Version has the words, “Know ye that he is nigh,” the Son of man, the King. His own nation rejected him when he came in mercy; so his next coming would be a time of terrible judgment and retribution to his guilty capital. Oh, that Jews and Gentiles today were wise enough to learn the lesson of that fiery trial, and to seek his face, those wrath they cannot bear!

[BODY] The King left his followers in no doubt as to when these things should happen: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass till all</sty>

--- PAGE 427 ---

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">these things be fulfilled.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>It<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>was just about the ordinary limit of a generation when the Roman armies compassed Jerusalem, whose measure of iniquity was then full, and overflowed in misery, agony, distress, and bloodshed such as the world never saw<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>before or since. Jesus was a true Prophet; everything that he foretold was literally fulfilled. He confirmed what he had already said, and what he was about to say, by a solemn affirmation: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>“The Word of the Lord endureth for ever,” and though that Lord appeared in fashion as a man, and was shortly to be crucified as a malefactor, his words would endure when heaven and earth would have fulfilled the purpose for which he had created them, and passed away.

[BODY] Christ’s promises of pardon are as sure of fulfilment as his prophecies of punishment; no word of his shall ever “pass away.”

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">36.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angeh of heaven, but my Father only.</sty>

[BODY] There is a manifest change in our Lord’s words here, which clearly indicates that they refer to his last great coming to judgment: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">But of that day and hour knoweth no man</sty>.” Some would be prophets have wrested this verse from its evident meaning by saying, “Though we do not know the day and the hour of Christ’s coming, we may know the year, the month, and even the week.” If this method of “renting the words of Jesus is not blasphemous, it is certainly foolish, and betrays disloyalty to the King. He added that, not only does no man know of that day and hour, but it is<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>hidden from angelic beings also: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">No, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>We need not therefore be troubled by idle prophecies of hair-brained fanatics, even if they claim to interpret the Scriptures; for what the angels do not know has not been revealed to them. Even Christ, in his human nature, so voluntarily limited his own capacities that he knew not the time of his Second Advent (Mark 13:32). It is enough for us to know that he will surely come; our great concern should be to be ready for his appearing whenever he shall return.

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 24:42-51</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE KING COMMANDS HIS SERVANTS TO WATCH</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">42.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.</sty>

[BODY] This is the practical conclusion of the whole matter. That our Lord is coming, is certain; that his coming may be at any moment, is a matter of faith; and that we are ignorant of the time of his coming, is a matter of fact<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">:</sty> “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Christ’s words are in the present tense. He does not say, “Ye know not what hour your Lord will<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>come,” but, “what hour your Lord doth come”, as if to keep us always expecting him; and lest we should not heed his words, he puts the command in plainest language:” <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Watch therefore.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>The title that he uses gives additional force to the command to his disciples to watch, for it is our <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Lord  </sty>who is coming quickly.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">43, 44.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  But know this, that if the goodman of the house had known in what watch the thief would come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken up. [BODY] If the householder has reliable information that a thief is coming, but does not know at what hour he will arrive, he will keep awake all night, waiting for his appearance; but if “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the goodman of the house</sty>” is<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>told “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">in what watch the thief</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>will<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>come, he will be specially on the alert at that time. Every little sound will attract his attention. He thinks he hears someone at the back door; no, the thief is trying to enter by a front window! Wherever he comes, he will find that the master’s ear is listening, the master’s eye is watching, the master’s hand is ready to arrest him; for he had received timely warning of the housebreaker’s coming. Men act thus wisely with

--- PAGE 431 ---

[BODY] regard to burglars; what a pity they are not equally wise in watching for the coming of their Lord! We do not know, we cannot even guess, in what watch of earth’s long night HE will come: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">In such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>There is the present tense again, “the Son of man cometh,” he is coming; his own words are, “Behold, I am <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">coming</sty> quickly.”

[BODY] Christ’s coming to the world will be like that of the thief, when it is not suspected or expected, and therefore when due preparations for his reception have not been made; but his true followers will not let “that day “overtake them “as a thief “(1 Thessalonians 5:4). ‘They ought ever to be looking for his appearing. Our Lord’s injunction to his disciples ought to have even greater weight with us who live so much nearer to the time of his Second Advent than it had with those to whom he addressed his warning words, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Therefore be ye also ready.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>We ought to be as watchful as if we knew that Christ would come tonight; because, although we do not know when he will come, we do know that he may come at any moment. Oh, to be ready for his appearing, watching and waiting for him as servants whose Lord has been long away from them, and who may return at any hour! This will not make us neglect our daily calling; on the contrary, we shall be all the more diligent in attending to our earthly duties because our hearts are at rest about our heavenly treasures.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">45, 46.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season? Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.</sty>

[BODY] The apostles were “stewards of the mysteries of God” (1 Corinthians 4:1), and “good stewards of the manifold grace of God” (1 Peter 4:10). One great qualification for a steward was that he should be found “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">faithful</sty>” both to “his lord” and to all in the<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">household</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>over whom he was “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">made ruler.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>It was needful also that he should be<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">wise</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>in his dealings with his fellow-servants; for, notwithstanding the honor put upon him, he was still a<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">servant</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>who must give to his lord an account of his stewardship. These words describe the service of a minister, preaching the truth with all his heart, and seeking “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">to give meat in due season</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>to all over whom

--- PAGE 432 ---

[BODY] the Holy Ghost hath made him an overseer. Or they picture a teacher, endeavoring to feed the minds of the young with sound doctrine; or they portray any servant of Christ, whatever his calling may be, doing the work that his Master has appointed him, just as he would wish to do it if he knew that his Lord was coming at that moment to examine it: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Blessed is thatwhom hi lord when he cometh shall find so doing.</sty>.” Such a servant of Christ is blessed; he is a happy man to be found by his Lord “so doing.” May our Master find us thus occupied when he cometh!

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">47.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Verily I say unto you, That he shall make him ruler over all his goods.</sty>

[BODY] His lord had formerly made him “ruler over his household”, the steward who had charge of all the household servants. His faithful and prudent conduct in that office won for him promotion to a higher post, so that his lord resolved <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">to  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">make him ruler over all his goods.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Thus is it among the servants of King Jesus, there are rewards for faithful service not of debt, but of grace; not according to the rule of the Law, but according to the discipline of the house of God, and the higher rule of Love.

[BODY] It should be noted that faithfulness in one form of service is rewarded by further service and increased responsibility. The servant, whose pound gained ten pounds, received authority over ten cities (Luke 19:17).

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">48-51.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But and if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; and shall begin to smite his fellowservants, and to eat and drink with the drunken; the lord of that servant shall come in a day when he looketh not for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of, and shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.</sty>

[BODY] This man was a “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">servant  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>so that<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>we have here a warning, not to the outside world, but to those who are inside the Church of Christ, and who profess to be servants of God. This is also specially a warning to ministers of the Word, those who are made rulers over God’s household. This man, though a servant, was <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">an  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">evil  </sty>servant”; a hypocrite, one who had

--- PAGE 433 ---

[BODY] intruded into an office which he had no right to occupy. His thoughts and words were evil: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">If that evil servant shall say in his heart, my lord delayeth his coming.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>His conduct towards those put under him was evil: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">and shall begin to smite his fellowservant.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>His own life was evil: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">and to eat and drink with the drunken.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>His evildoing would be suddenly cut short by his master’s appearance: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">The lord of that servant shall come in a day when he looketh not for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Immediate and terrible punishment would be meted out to him: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">And shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites:</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>he was one of them, he pretended to be a servant of God when all the while he was a slave of Satan, serving self and sin; let him go to his own company. He was really cut in two before, outwardly he was a follower of Christ, inwardly he served his own lusts; to “cut him asunder” will only be a righteous perpetuation of his own double-faced character. Will that be the end of him? No; “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">there shall be weeping and: gnashing of teeth.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>What a<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>“portion” for one who was numbered amongst God’s servants! As we read of it, let us, in deep humility, remember the solemn injunction of the apostle, “Let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.”
