[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 25:1-13</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE KING AND HIS MARRIAGE PROCESSION</sty>

[BODY] Our Lord was still seated, with his disciples, upon the Mount of Olives (see chapter 24:3). The instructive parable that follows was spoken by him in continuation of the discourse we have been considering. It is evidently intended to set forth, under a familiar figure, the need of preparation for the King’s glorious appearing when he comes to claim his bride. To those of us who will not be alive at Christ’s Second Advent, the midnight cry, “Go ye out to meet him,” will sound forth at the hour of death.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">1.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="0"> THEN shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins, which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom. And five of them were wise, and five were foolish.</sty>

[BODY] According to Oriental custom, the bridegroom is represented as having gone to the house of his bride’s father, whence he would conduct his spouse to her future home. The parable opens at the point where some of his professed friends are waiting to join the procession, and go in with him to the marriage-feast. Thus is the nominal Church of Christ waiting for the coming of the Lord. There did not seem to be much difference in the eternal appearance of the “ten virgins, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They were all virgins, they all took their lamps, and they all went forth to meet the bridegroom. They all made a profession of attachment to him, which led them to separate themselves from their other companions and acquaintances, that they might go forth to meet him on his wedding-night.

[BODY] There was, however, a vital and essential difference between them: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Five of them were wise, and five were foolish.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Let us fain hope that we are not to gather from our Lord’s words that one half of the professing Church is composed of those whom he calls “foolish.” Yet our Savior would not have spoken of so great a proportion if there were not really a very large

--- PAGE 435 ---

[BODY] admixture of foolish professors with the wise possessors of the grace of God.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">3.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Them that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them:</sty>

[BODY] They may have thought that, if they had lamps that were similar to those carried by others, it would be sufficient. Perhaps they judged that the secret store of oil, being unseen, was unnecessary. They were willing to carry a lamp in one hand; but to devote the other hand to the care of an oil-flask, was more than they were willing to do. It is the want of the oil of grace that is<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>the fatal flaw in many a professor’s lamp. Many have a name to live, but have not the life of God within their souls. They make a profession of attachment to Christ, but they have not the inward supply of the Spirit of grace to keep it up. There is a glitter or a flash, but there is no permanent light, and there cannot be any, for although they <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">have</sty> “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">lamps</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>they have “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">no oil with them.</sty>”

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">4.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.</sty>

[BODY] They had oil in their lamps, and oil with their lamps. Lamps are of no use without oil; yet the oil needs the lamp, or it will not be used. Grace should reveal its presence, faith in Christ should be avowed; but it is worse than useless to make a profession of love to Christ, unless there is a secret store of grace by which the external part of religion may be maintained even before the allsearching eye of the King himself. Unless the Spirit of God be in us, indeed, and of a truth, we may for a while make a fair show in the flesh, but the end will be the blackness of darkness for ever.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">5.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">While the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept.</sty>

[BODY] How sadly true it is, that, in the history of Christ’s Church, genuine saints and mere professors have often “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">slumbered and slept</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>side by<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>side! Those who have the oil of grace are not always wide awake to serve their Master, and watch for his appearing. In the case of even true believers, the delay in Christ’s coming causes disappointment, weariness, and lethargy; and his Church falls fast asleep, when she ought to be watching for her

--- PAGE 436 ---

[BODY] Lord. As for the “foolish “, whether self-deceived or hypocrites, there being no true life of God in the soul, after a while their apparent earnestness disappears, and Satan drugs them into a fatal slumber.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">6.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him.</sty>

[BODY] That midnight cry, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Behold, the bridegroom cometh,</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>startled all the sleepers. It should be well if we all I thought more of the great truth of our Lord’s Second Advent. The oftener it is preached, in due proportion with other revealed doctrines, the more likely will it be to arouse both slumbering possessors and sleeping professors of love to Christ. As the midnight of this present evil age approaches, there is increasing need for all to be bidden to listen for the clarion cry, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Go ye out to meet him.</sty>”

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">7.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps.</sty>

[BODY] The suddenness of the alarm made them all start to their feet, and begin to examine and trim their lamps. They could not go to meet the bridegroom without carrying a light; that was an essential part of their preparation for joining the King’s marriage procession. Those virgins who had “oil in their vessels with their lamps” soon finished their trimming, and were ready to start; but those who had “lamps” but “no oil” were unable to perform the neceesary trimming. It is a pity that any should have to be trimming their lamps when they come to die, or when the sign of the Son of man appears in the heaven; but if that work is attempted without the Spirit or the grace of God, it will be an eternal failure.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">8.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are aone out.</sty>

[BODY] They now began to value what they had aforetime despised; they had been so foolish as to think that oil was unnecessary, now they saw that it was the one thing needful. Hence their request to their wiser companions: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Give us of your oil.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They gave a dreadful reason for their request: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">for our lamps are gone out,</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>or<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">, going out;  </sty>the dry<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>wick fickered a while, and then died out in darkness, like the snuff of a candle.

--- PAGE 437 ---


[BODY] Those are terrible words, “our lamps are gone out.” It is worse to have a lamp that has gone out than never to have had a lamp at all. “Our lamps are gone out.” The foolish virgins seemed to say, “We thought everything was ready for tonight, we even gloried in our lamps, we promised ourselves a bright future, we thought all was well for our share in the marriage-supper; but our lamps aro gone out, and we have no oil with which to supply them.” May no reader of this page ever have to utter this bitter lament!

[BODY] Those who are putting of their repentance till their dying hour are like these foolish virgins; their folly has reached its utmost height. When the death-sweat lies cold on the brow, the neglected oil of grace will be valued. Then will come the despairing cry “Send for a minister to pray for me, get in some Christian people to see what they can do for me.”

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">9.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves,</sty>

[BODY] No believer has more grace than he needs: “the wise” virgins had no oil to give away. They gave the best advice they could under the circumstances, although it was of no avail<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">:  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>There is a<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>proper place where the oil can be bought at the right time: we are bidden to “buy the truth,” grace is sold in God’s market on gospel terms, “without money, and without price;” but when the midnight cry is heard, the day of grace has closed, and buying and selling are over for ever.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">10.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut.</sty>

[BODY] Undoubtedly, there are death-bed repentances; but it is to be feared that, in the great majority of cases, people who wake up so late to a true conviction of their condition will find that, while they go to buy the longdespised grace, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the bridegroom</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>will<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>come. The poor head may be

--- PAGE 438 ---

[BODY] so distracted with pain that the mind may not be able to catch the idea of what faith in Christ is; mental capacity may wholly fail in that dread hour. The risk is so great that none but the fatally foolish will postpone till then the preparation for the King’s coming.

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">They that were ready went in with him to the marriage:</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>their readiness consisted in having lighted lamps, or flaming torches; our preparation for death or Christ’s coming, is the possession of grace in the heart. “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">And the door was shut:</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>when<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>that door is once shut, it will never be opened. There are some who dote and dream about an opening of that door, after death, for those who have died impenitent; but there is nothing in the Scriptures to warrant such an expectation. Any “larger hope” than that revealed in the Word of God, is a delusion and a snare.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">11, 12.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, lord, lord, open to us. But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.</sty>

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">The other virgins</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>were not “ready” when the bridegroom came; and there is no hint in the parable that they were any more ready when they came and clamored at his closed door, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Lord, lord, open to us</sty>.’ “We came to meet thee, we carried lamps, we were with the other virgins; Lord, Lord, open to us! “His answer tolled the knell of any vain hope of admission that they might have cherished: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Verily, I say unto you, I know you  </sty>not.” “If any man loveth God, the same is known of him.” (1 Corinthians 8:3, R.V.) The Good Shepherd says, “I know mine own, and mine own know me.” (John 10:14, R.V.) Those whom Jesus Christ knows in this sense, he loves; and they love him because he has first loved them. The foolish virgins had professed to be the bridegroom’s friends, yet they were proved to be not even his acquaintances. May none of us ever hear from the blessed lips of the heavenly Bridegrooom that terrible death-sentence, “I know you not”!

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">13.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.</sty>

[BODY] Our Lord again enjoins upon his followers the duty of watchfulness, as in

--- PAGE 439 ---

[BODY] chapter 24:42; and repeats, in a slightly-altered form, the reason previously given: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">For ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>It is<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>idle to say that we may find out the year, if not the day and hour, of Christ’s coming. The time of the end is hidden, and shall not be known until sudden1;s he shall appear “in the clouds of heaven in power and great glory.” It should be our one great concern to be sure that we shall be ready to meet him whenever he may come.

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 25:14-30</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE PARABLE OF THE TALENTS</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">14, 15.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods. And unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability; and straight way took his journey.</sty>

[BODY] Our Savior had been speaking of himself as the heavenly Bridegroom; now he compares himself to “a <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">man travelling into a far country.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>The word “travelling” suggests that our Lord has only gone away for a season and that he will return when his purpose in going into the “far country” is accomplished. When he went back from earth to heaven, it was a long journey; but he did not leave his servants without needful supplies during his absence. He “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">called his own servants</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>his bondservants, his household serntors; “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">and delivered unto them his goods.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>The servants were his, and the goods also were his; his slaves could not claim as their own either their persons or their possessions; all belonged to their lord, and were to be used for him.

[BODY] He did not entrust to all the same quantity of goods: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability</sty>.” He was the judge of the ability of each of his servants, and he made no mistake in his allotment of the talents to them. We may rest assured, if we are the Lord’s servants, that he has bestowed upon us as many talents as we can rightly use, and quite as many as we shall be able to account for when he returns. The all-important matter for us is to be faithful to the trust committed to us.

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">And straightway took his journey:  </sty>“our Lord knew all that was to happen before he left the earth, — his passion, crucifixion, and resurrection; but he calmly talked of it as a man might speak of his

--- PAGE 441 ---

[BODY] preparations for travelling into a foreign country. He has gone, and his servants are left behind to make the best use they can of his ascension-gifts while he is absent.

[BODY] This parable, like that of the ten virgins, has to do with real and nominal Christians, with all who are or who profess to be the servants of Christ. The “talents” are anything and everything that our Lord has given to us for use here as his stewards.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">16-18.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then he that had received the five talents went and traded with the same, and made them other five talents. And likewise he that had received two, he also gained other two. But he that had received one went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord’s money.</sty>

[BODY] It is very significant that our Savior said that “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">he that had receired one</sty>” talent<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord’s money.</sty>” Many who have<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">five talents</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>or “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">two</sty>” have not “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">traded with the same,</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>and so gained “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">other five</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>or<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">other two</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">;  </sty>but Jesus knew that it was the servant with one talent who was most exposed to the temptation to do nothing because he could only do n little. There are perile connected with the possession of five talents, or two; but the man who has only one talent is in equal if not greater danger. Let us all remember that, as it is a sin to hide one talent in the earth, it is a greater sin to hide two or five talents. It was “his lord’s money” that the slothful servant hid. It would have been wrong to bury what belonged to himself; but he was doubly blameworthy in hiding that which had been entrusted to him by his lord, instead of trading with it so as to increase it. Are any of us thus sinning against our Savior?

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">19.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">After a long time the lord of those servants cometh, and reckoneth with them.</sty>

[BODY] There is a reckoning-day coming, even though “a long time “may elapse before “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the lord of those servants cometh.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Jesus is coming back from the far country whither he has gone; his own word is, “Behold, I come quickly.” We must not leave this great fact out of our reckoning; and as his

--- PAGE 442 ---

[BODY] stewards, we must be prepared at any moment for him to come and reckon with us as to the talents with which he has endowed each of his servants.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">20, 21.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And so he that had received five talents came and brought other five talents, saying, lord, thou deliveredet unto me, five talents: behold, I have gained beside them five talents more. His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou haet been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.</sty>

[BODY] Have all of us, who “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">received five talents</sty>” from our Lord, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">gained beside them five talents more</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">?</sty> I trow not. Have we double the grace we had at first? Twice the tact with which we began our service for God? Twofold adaptation to the work he has given us to do? It was so with this servant; and therefore, his lord commended and rewarded him. There was no proportion between his service and its reward<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">:  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>He who is faithful to his Lord shall have greater opportunities of proving his loyalty and devotion in a higher sphere; and in addition, he shall share the bliss of his Lord’s return<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">:  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Enter thou into the joy of thy lord.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>This is not the servant’s portion, but the Master’s portion shared with his faithful servants. This will be the consummation of all heavenly delights; not so much that we shall have a joy of our own as that we shall enter into the joy of our Lord.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">22, 23.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  He also that had received two talent, came and said, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me two talents: behold, I have gained two other talents beside them. [BODY] This servant’s commendation and reward are exactly the same as those given to his more highly privileged brother; as if our Savior would teach us that it is not the number of our talents, but the use we make of them, that is the essential matter. [CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 25:31-46</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE ROYAL AND UNIVERSAL JUDGE</sty>

[BODY] Here we have the King’s own description of the Day of Judgment; and in the solemn silence of our spirits we may well put off our shoes from our feet as we draw nigh to this holy ground.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">31.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">When the Son of man shall come inhis glory and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory:</sty>

[BODY] Our Savior had a wonderful series of contrasts passing before his eye as he uttered this sublime prophecy.

[BODY] Within three days he was to be crucified; ;yet he spoke of the time “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">When the Son of man shall come in his glory.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>He had with him a little company of disciples, one of whom would betray him, another would deny him, and all would forsake him; yet by faith he saw the heavenly retinue that would attend him at his coming: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">and all the holy angels with him.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Wearied and worn with his labors, and saddened because of the hardness of men’s hearts and the impending doom of Jerusalem, he sat on the slope of the Mount of Olives; but his thoughts were projected across the ages as he told his hearers of the glorious throne he would occupy in the day when he should return as the Royal and Universal Judge of mankind: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>The great white throne shall be set on high, all pure and lustrous, bright and clear as a polished mirror, in which every man shall see himself and his sins reflected; and on that throne shall sit “the Son of man.” Behind the Kingly Judge, “all the holy angels” shall be ranged, rank on rank, an innumerable and glorious body-guard, to grace the court of their enthroned Lord on the day of the last great assize; and, at his bidding, to remove from his presence all whom he shall condemn.

--- PAGE 447 ---

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">32, 33.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats: and he shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.</sty>

[BODY] In the last great day of the Lord, all nations that have ever existed on the face of the globe shall be gathered before the judgment-seat of Christ. The earth, which is now becoming more and more one vast graveyard or channel-house, shall yield up her dead; and the sea itself, transformed into a solid pavement, shall bear upon its bosom the millions who lie hidden in its gloomy caverns. All mankind will be aseembled before their Judge: “and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall fail because of him.” At first they will be gathered together in one heterogeneous mass; but the myriad multitude will speedily be divided into two companies: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">and he shall separate them one from another.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>The King will be the divider in that dread day. How he will separate them, no one can tell, except that it will be “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Not one goat will be left among the sheep, nor one sheep with the goats. The division will bo very close and personal: “one from another.” They will not be separated into nations, nor even into families; but each individual will be allotted his or her proper place among the sheep or among the goats.

[BODY] “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">And he shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>There will be only two companies, one on the right hand of the Judge, and the other on his left. The Lord Jesus Christ “shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing “; and all who will be summoned before his dread tribunal will be either alive from the dead, or still dead in trespasses and sins. There will be no middle company in that day, as in God’s sight there is no third class even now. All our names are either in the Lamb’s Book of Life or in the Judge’s Book of Death.

[BODY] Some have taught that the judgment here foretold is that of the professing Church, and not of the whole world. There may be some ground for their belief; yet it seems impossible to apply the full meaning of our Savior’s majestic words to any scene except the general judgment of the whole human race.

--- PAGE 448 ---


[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">34.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for youirom the foundation of the world:</sty>

[BODY] Turning first to the chosen company on his right hand, the “great multitude, which no man could number,” the King will say to them, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Come.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They had accepted his previous invitation, “Come unto me; “now he gives them another and a more glorious “Come,” which was, however, included in the former one; for when he said, “I will give you rest,” heaven itself was promised to them. The King calls his loved ones by a choice name: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">ye blessed of my Father.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>We shall not know what bliss that title implies until we hear it from our Savior’s lips; and even then we shall only begin to understand what we shall continue to enjoy throughout eternity.

[BODY] All true believers are joint-heirs with Jesus Christ, so the King will next say to them, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>The “inheritance, incorruptible, and unclefiled, and that fadeth not away,” is the inalienable right of all who are made kings and priests unto God; and that which has been prepared for them from the foundation of the world must be possessed by them when the world itself has answered the end of its creation, and has been burned up.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">35, 36.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  For I was an hungred and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prision, and ye came unto me.</sty>

[BODY] The King dwells with great delight upon the details of his servants’ kindnesses to himself. Are we, then, after all, to be saved by our works? By no means. Yet are our works the evidences of our being saved. If our actions are such as Christ will commend at the day of judgment, they prove that we are saved by grace, and that the Holy Spirit has wrought effectually in us, and through us. The services mentioned by the King were all rendered to himself: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat,: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger and ye took</sty>

--- PAGE 449 ---

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">me in: naked and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prision, and ye came unto me.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>There is no mention of what the righteous had said, or of what profession of love to Ghrist they had made; the commendation was for what the King declared they had actually done by way of ministering unto him.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">37-39.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hugred and fed thee? [BODY] They will bashfully disclaim the praise pronounced by the King. They had no idea that there was anything meritorious in what they had done; they never dreamed of being rewarded for it. When the saints stand before the judgment seat, the bare thought of there being any excellence in what they have done will be new to them, for they have formed a very lowly estimate of their own performances. They fed the hungry, clothed the naked, visited the sick, for Christ’s sake, because it was the sweetest thing in the world to do anything for Jesus. They did it because they delighted to do it, because they could not help doing it, because their new nature impelled them to it.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">40.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And. the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily, I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.</sty>

[BODY] Christ has much more to do with his brethren’s sorrow than we sometimes think. Are they hungry? He puts it, “I was an hungred.” Do they thirst? He says, “I was thirsty.” The sympathy of Christ is continuous, and all adown the ages he will perpetually incarnate himself in the suffering bodies of his tried and afflicted people. Hence the opportunity of doing him service so long as we are here.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">41.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels.</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">42, 43.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  For I was an hungred, and ye gave me no meat: I wus thirsty, and ye gave me no drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me not in: naked, and ye clothed me not: sick, and in prison, and ye visited me not.</sty>

Yet, even then, some will try to justify themselves.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">44.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then shall they also answer him, saying Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, or athirst, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not mtnister unto thee</sty>

[BODY] What a deceiver is sin! How presumptuous, that even in the presence of the Omniscient Judge, it denies its own real character; and makes its votaries pretend to have attained to the divine standard of holiness!

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">45.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then shall he answer them, saying Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of thee, ye did it not to me.</sty>

--- PAGE 451 ---

[BODY] Our Lord does not mean to teach that men will be condemned because they have not been charitable to the poor and needy, or that they will be saved if they are generous and openhanded. That would indeed be salvation by works, to be boasted of to all eternity. He does mean that only those who produce such fruit as this prove that “the root of the matter” is in them; by ministering to his poor brethren, out of love to him, they show that they are the subjects of that distinguishing grace which makes them differ from others. All our future depends upon our relationslip to the Lord Jesus Christ.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">46.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.</sty>

Between heaven and hell there is a great gulf fixed, an awfu1 abyss that cannot be crossed, so that the separation between the sheep and the goats will be eternal and unalterable. God grant that none of us may be on the wrong side of that great gulf!

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 26:6-13</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE KING ANOINTED FOR HIS BURIAL</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">6, 7.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Now when Jesus was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, there came unto him a woman having an alabaster box of very precious ointment, and poured it on his head, he sat at meat.</sty>

[BODY] We do not know who <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Simon the leper  </sty>was, nor whether this <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">woman</sty> was Mary, the sister of Lazarus, though I believe she was the one who came to Jesus, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">having an alabaster box of very precious ointment, and poured it on his head,  </sty>as he sat at<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  meat.  </sty>The beauty of this woman’s act consisted in this, that it was all for Christ. [BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">8, 9.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  But when his disciples saw it, they had indignation saying, To what purpose is this waste? For this ointment might have been sold for much, and given to the poor.</sty>

[BODY] When you do the best you can do, from the purest motives, and your Lord accepts your service, do not expect that your brethren will approve all your actions. If you do, you will be greatly dianppointed. There was never a more beautiful proof of love to Christ than this anointing at Bethany; yet the disciples found fault with it: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">they had indignation, saying,  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">To what purpose is this waste? If this devoted and enthusiastic woman had waited for the advice of these prudent people, she would neither have sold the ointment, nor

--- PAGE 455 ---

[BODY] poured it out. She did well to take counsel with her own loving heart, and then to pour the precious nard upon that dear head which was so<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>soon to be crowned with thorns. She thus showed that there was, at least, one heart in the world that thought nothing was too good for her Lord! and that the best of the best ought to bo given to him. May she have many imitators in every age until Jesus comes again!

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">10. </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">When Jesus understood it, he said unto them, Why trouble ye the woman she hath wrought a good work upon me.</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">11. </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">For ye have the poor always with you; but me ye have not always.</sty>

[BODY] Our Lord always cared for the poor; he was himself poor, he was the poor people’s Preacher, he fed the hungry poor, and healed the sick poor. [BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">12, 13.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">For in that she hath poured this oinmentt my body, she did it for my burial. --- PAGE 456 ---

[BODY] She probably did not know all that her action meant when she anointed her Lord for his burial. The consequences of the simplest action done for Christ may be much greater than we think. Go thou, my sister, and do what God bids thee; and it shall be seen that thou hast done far more than thou knowest. Obey the holy impulse within thy spirit, my brother; and thou mayest do ten thousand I times more than thou hast ever I imagined to be possible.

[BODY] This woman’s outburst of affection, this simple-hearted act of love to Christ himself, is one of those things which are to live as long as the gospel lives. The aroma of this loving deed is to abide as long as the world itself endures.

[BODY] Great sorrow produces different results in different persons. In the Savior’s case, it aroused him to an awful agony of earnestness in prayer; in the disciples’ case, it sent them to sleep. [BODY] Whether Judas bought the <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">field  </sty>in which he committed suicide (Acts 1:18), or whether <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the chief priests,  </sty>hearing how he meant to spend <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the pieces of silver,  </sty>carried out his intention, makes no real difference in the result. <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">The field of blood  </sty>became the perpetual memorial of the infamy of Judas. When he sold his Lord, he little thought what would be done with the money received as the price of the betrayal. In the fullest sense possible, he was guilty of the blood of the Lord; that blood was upon him, not to seal his pardon, but to confirm his condemnation.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">9, 10.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying, And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was valued, whom they of the children of Israel did value; and gave them for the potters field, as the lord appointed me.</sty>

[BODY] Even the disposal of <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the thirty pieces of silver  </sty>fulfilled an ancient prophecy. The dark sayings of the prophets as well as their brighter utterances shall all be proved to be true as, one by one, they come to maturity.

[BODY] The fate of Judas should be a solemn warning to all professing Christians, and especially to all ministers. He was one of the twelve apostles, yet he was a son of perdition, and in the end he went to his own place. Each of us has his own place, heaven or hell; which is it?

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 27:11-26</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">JESUS: PILATE: BARABBAS</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">11. </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And Jesus stood before the governor: and the governor asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And Jesus said unto him, Thou sayest.</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Jesus  </sty>did not look much like a king as he stood before Pilate; there was little enough of the robes of royalty about his simple apparel. Yet even in his humiliation there must have been so much of majesty that even <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the governor  </sty>was prompted to ask, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">art thou the King of the Jews?</sty>” There was no longer any reason why the King should conceal his true position, so he answered, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Thou sayest.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>“It is even as thou sayest, I am the King of the Jews.” The Jews rejected their King: “He came unto his own, and his own received him not.” Yet was he their King although they refused to bow before his sceptre of grace and mercy.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">12-14.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And when he was accused of the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing. [BODY] This was the time for Jesus to be dumb, “like a sheep before her shearers.” His silence astonished Pilate, as his speech had before overawed the officers sent to arrest him (John 7:45, 46). Jesus <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">answered nothing,  </sty>for he was there as his people’s representative; and though he had not sinned, they were guilty of all that was falsely laid to his charge. He might have cleared himself of every accusation that was brought against him, but that would have left the load of guilt upon those whose place he came to take; so <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">he answered never a word.  </sty>Such silence was<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>sublime.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">15-18.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Now at that feast the governor was wont to release unto the people a prisoner, whom they would. [BODY] Pilate was really anxious to deliver Christ from his cruel enemies; but; like most wicked men, he was a great coward, so he attempted to gain his end by a crafty artifice. <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">He knew that for envy they had delivered him;</sty> and he may have hoped that Jesus was so popular among the people that an appeal to the masses would result in a verdict in Christ’s favor, especially as the choice of one to be released lay between “the King of the Jews “and a notoriously wicked man, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Barabbas.  </sty>Surely they would ask for their King to be set at liberty! Pilate little knew the sway the chief priests had over the populace, nor the fickleness of the crowds, whose jubilant cry of “Hosanna! “would so soon be changed to hoarse shouts of “Away with him! Crucify him!”

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">19.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">When he was set down on the judgment seat, his wife sent unto him, saying, Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.</sty>

[BODY] Here was an unlooked-for witness to the innocence of Christ. Whether the <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">dream of Pilate’s wife  </sty>was a divine revelation of Christ’s glory or not, we cannot tell; but the message sent by her to the governor must have made him even more anxious than before to release Jesus.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">20-22.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">But the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude that they should ask Barabbas, and destroy Jesus. [BODY] Now the die is cast, the choice of <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the multitude is  </sty>made; <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Barabbas  </sty>is preferred before Jesus. The Lord of glory had been sold by Judas for the

--- PAGE 485 ---

[BODY] price of a slave; and now a robber, a murderer, and a leader in sedition, is a greater favorite with the people than the Prince of life. Were there no voices raised in Christ’s favor? Were there none out of all that multitude whose sick he had healed, whoso hunger he had satisfied, who would remember him in that day, and ask that he might be spared? No, not one; there were none in the crowd silently sympathising with the Savior; they <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">all  </sty>said<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">,  </sty>“<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Let him be crucified.</sty>”

[BODY] A blind, unreasoning hate had taken possession of the people. They gave no answer to Pilate’s wondering enquiry, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Why, what evil hath he done?</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>for he had done nothing amiss; they only repeated the brutal demand, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Let him be crucified.</sty>”

[BODY] The world’s hatred of Christ is shown in similar fashion today. He has done no evil, no one has suffered harm at his hands, all unite to pronounce him innocent; and yet they practically cry, “Away with him! Crucify him!”

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">24.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it.</sty>

[BODY] Ah! Pilate, you need something stronger than <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">water  </sty>to wash <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the blood  </sty>of that <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">just person  </sty>off your <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">hands.  </sty>You cannot rid yourself of responsibility by that farce. He who has power to prevent a wrong is guilty of the act if he permits others to do it, even though he does not actually commit it himself.

[BODY] Pilate joined with all the other witnesses in declaring that Jesus was “just “or “righteous.” He even went so far as to declare, “I find in him no fault at all” (John 8:38).

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">25.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then answered all the people, and said, His blood be on us, and on our children.</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">All the people  </sty>willingly took upon themselves the guilt of the murder of our dear Lord: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">His blood be on us, and on our children.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>This fearful imprecation must have been remembered by many when the soldiers of Titus spared neither age nor sex, and the Jewish capital became the veritable Aceldama, the field of blood. [BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">26.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then released he Barabbas unto them: and when he had encourged Jesus he delivered him to be crucified.</sty>

[BODY] The Roman scourging was one of the most terrible punishments to which anyone could be subjected. The Jewish beating with rods was a mild chastisement compared with the brutal flagellation by the imperial lictors; yet even this our Lord endured for our sakes. Yet the scourging was but the beginning of the awful end: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">When he had scourged Jesus, he delivered him to be crucified.  </sty>Knowing him to be innocent, Pilate first scourged him, and then gave him up to the fury of his fanatical foes.

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 27:27-31</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE KING MOCKED BY THE SOLDIERS</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">27-30.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the common hall, and gathered unto him the whole band of soldiers. And they stripped him, and put on him a scarlet robe. [BODY] Ridicule is very painful to bear. In our Savior’s case, there was great cruelty mixed with mockery. These Roman <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">soldiers</sty> were men to whom bloodshed was amusement; and now that there was given up into their hands one who was charged with making himself a king, we can conceive what a subject for jest the gentle Jesus was in their esteem. They were not touched by the gentleness of his manner, nor by his sorrowful countenance; but they sought to invent all manner of scorn, to pour on his devoted head. Surely the world never saw a more marvellous scene than the King of kings thus derided as a mimic monarch by the meanest of men. <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">The whole band of soldiers was gathered unto him</sty>, for seldom was such sport provided in <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the common hall.  </sty>Jesus is a king, so he must wear the garb of royalty: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">they stripped him, and put on him a scarlet robe,</sty> some old soldier’s scarlet or purple coat. The king must be crowned: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">when they had platted a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head.  </sty>He must sway a sceptre: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">a reed in his right hand.  </sty>Homage must be paid to him: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">and they bowed the knee before him.  </sty>Cruel men! Yet probably they knew no better.

[BODY] Oh, that we were half as inventive in devising honor for our King as these soldiers were in planning his dishonor! Let us render to Christ the real homage that these men pretended to offer him. Let us crown him Lord of all, and in truest loyalty bow the knee, and hail him, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">King</sty>.”

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">31.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And after that they had mocked him, they took the robe off from him, and put his own raiment on him, and led him away to crucify him.</sty>

[BODY] It was divinely overruled that Jesus should go forth with his <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">own raiment on him,  </sty>that nobody might say that another person had been substituted for the Savior. As they <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">led him away,  </sty>robed in that well-known seamless garment, woven from the top throughout, all who looked upon him would say, “It is the Nazarene going forth to execution; we recognize his dress as well as his person.”

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 27:32-38</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">THE KING CRUCIFIED</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">32.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And as they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name; him they compelled to bear his cross.</sty>

[BODY] Perhaps they were afraid that Christ would die from exhaustion; so they <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">compelled Simon to bear his cross,  </sty>Any one of Christ’s followers might have wished to have been this <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">man of Cyrene;  </sty>but we need not envy him, for there is a cross for each of us to carry. Oh, that we were as willing to bear Christ’s cross as Christ was to bear our sins on his cross! If anything happens to us by way of persecution or ridicule for our Lord’s sake, and the gospel’s, let us cheerfully endure it. As knights are made by a stroke from the sovereign’s sword, so shall we become princes in Christ’s realm as he lays his cross on our shoulders.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">33, 34.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull, They gave him vinegar to drink mingled with gall: and when he had tasted thereof, he would not drink.</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Golgotha  </sty>was the common place of execution for malefactors, the Tyburn or Old Bailey of Jerusalem, outside the gate of the city. There was a special symbolical reason for Christ’s suffering without the gate, and his followers are bidden to “go forth unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach “(Hebrews 13:11-13).

[BODY] A stupefying draught was given to the condemned, to take away something of the agony of crucifixion; but our Lord came to suffer, and he would not take anything that would at all impair his faculties. He did not forbid his fellow-sufferers drinking the <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">vinegar mingled with gall (</sty>“wine mingled with myrrh,” Mark 15:23), but <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">he would not drink thereof.</sty> Jesus did not refuse this draught because of its bitterness, for he was prepared to drink even to the last dreadful dregs the bitter cup of wrath

--- PAGE 490 ---

[BODY] which was his people’s due.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">35.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And they crucifiied him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.</sty>

[BODY] There is a world of meaning in that short sentence, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">and they crucified him,  </sty>driving their bolts of iron through his blessed hands and feet, fastening him to the cross, and lifting him up to hang there upon a gibbet reserved for felons. We can scarcely realize all that the crucifixion meant to our dear Lord; but we can join in Father’s prayer,—

[CENTERED] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">“</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">Lord Jesus! may we love and weep, Since thou for us art crucified.</sty><sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">”</sty>

[BODY] Then was fulfilled all that our Lord had foretold in Chapter 20:17-19, except his resurrection, the time for which had not arrived.

[BODY] The criminals’ clothes were the executioners’ perquisite. The Roman soldiers who crucified Christ had no thought of fulfilling the Scriptures when <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">they parted his garments, casting lots;  </sty>yet their action was exactly that which had been foretold in Psalm 22:18. The seamless robe would have been spoiled if it had been rent, so the soldiers raffled for the <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">veature  </sty>while they shared the other <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">garments  </sty>of our Lord. The dice would be almost stained with the blood of Christ, yet the gamblers played on beneath the shadow of his cross. Gambling is the most hardening of all vices. Beware of it in any form! No games of chance should be played by Christians, for the blood of Christ seems to have bespattered them all.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">36.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And sitting down they watched him there;</sty>

[BODY] Some watched him from curiosity, some to make sure that he really did die, some even delighted their cruel eyes with his sufferings; and there were some, hard by the cross, who wept and bewailed, a sword passing through their own hearts while the Son of man was agonizing even unto death

--- PAGE 491 ---


[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">37.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And set up over his head his accusation written, </sty><sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="1">THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">.</sty>

[BODY] What a marvellous providence it was that moved Pilate’s pen! The representative of the Roman emperor was little likely to concede kingship to any man; yet he deliberately wrote, THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS, and nothing would induce him to alter what he had written. Even on his cross, Christ was proclaimed King, in the sacerdotal Hebrew, the classical Greek, and the common Latin, so that everybody in the crowd could read the inscription.

[BODY] When will the Jews own Jesus as their King? They will do so one day, looking on him whom they pierced. Perhaps they will think more of Christ when Christians think more of them; when our hardness of heart towards them has gone, possibly their hardness of heart towards Christ may also disappear.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">38.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Then were there two thieves crucified with him, one on the right hand, and another on the left.</sty>

[BODY] As if to show that they regarded Christ as the worst of the three criminals, they put him between the <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">two thieves,  </sty>giving him the place of dishonor. Thus was the prophecy fulfilled, “He was numbered with the tranegressors.” The two malefactors deserved to die, as one of them admitted (Luke 23:40, 41); but a greater load of guilt rested upon Christ, for “He bare the sin of many,” and therefore he was rightly distinguished as the King of sufferers, who could truly ask,—

[CENTERED] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">“</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">Was ever grief like mine?</sty><sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">”</sty>

[CENTERED_H2] <sty c="0000d4" i="0" b="0">CHAPTER 27:39-49</sty>

[CENTERED] <sty c="006411" i="0" b="1">MOCKING THE CRUCIFIED KING</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">39, 40.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  And they that passed by reviled him, wagging their heads, and saying, thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save thyself. If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.</sty>

[BODY] Nothing torments a man when in pain more than mockery. When Jesus Christ most wanted words of pity and looks of kindness, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">they that passed by reviled him, wagging their heads.  </sty>Perhaps the most painful part of ridicule is to have one’s most solemn sayings turned to scorn, as were our Lord’s words about the temple of his body: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save thyself.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>He might have saved himself, he might have “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">come down from the cross;</sty> “but if he had done so, we could never have become the sons of God. It was because he was the Son of God that he did not come down from the cross, but hung there until he had completed the sacrifice for his people’s sin. Christ’s cross is the Jacob’s ladder by which we mount up to heaven.

[BODY] This is the cry of the Socinians today, “Come down from the cross. Give up the atoning sacrifice, and we will be Christians.” Many are willing to believe in Christ, but not in Christ crucified. They admit that he was a good man and a great teacher; but by rejecting his vicarious atonement, they practically un-Christ the Christ, as these mockers at Golgotha did.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">41-43.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Likewise also the chief priests mocking him, with the scribes and elders, said, He saved others; himself he cannot save. [BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">The chief priests, with the scribes and elders,  </sty>forgetting their high

--- PAGE 493 ---

[BODY] station and rank, joined the ribald crew in mocking Jesus in his death pangs. Every word was emphatic; every syllable cut and pierced our Lord to the heart. They mocked him as a Savior: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">He saved others; himself he cannot save</sty>.” They mocked him as a King: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and, we will believe him.</sty>” They mocked him as a believer: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">He trusted in God; let him deliver him now, if he will have him.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>They mocked him as the Son of God: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">For he said, I am the Son of God.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>Those who say that Christ was a good man virtually admit his deity, for he claimed to be the Son of God. If he was not what he professed to be, he was an impostor. Notice the testimony that Christ’s bitterest enemies bore even as they reviled him: “He saved others;” “He is the King of Israel” (R.V.); “He trusted in God.”

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">44.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">The thieves also, which were crucified with him, cast the same in his teeth.</sty>

[BODY] The sharers of his misery, the abjects who were crucified with him, joined in reviling Jesus. Nothing was wanting to fill up his cup of suffering and shame. The conversion of the penitent thief was all the more remarkable because he had but a little while before been amongst the mockers of his Savior. What a trophy of divine grace he became!

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">45.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour.</sty>

[BODY] Some have thought that this darkness covered the whole world, and so caused even a heathen to exclaim, “Either the world is about to expire, or the God who made the world is in anguish.” This darkness was supernatural; it was not an eclipse. The sun could no longer look upon his Maker surrounded by those who mocked him. He covered his face, and travelled on in tenfold night, in very shame that the great Sun of righteousness should himself be in such terrible darkness.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">46.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, My God, why hast thou forsaken me?</sty>

--- PAGE 494 ---

[BODY] In order that the sacrifice of Christ might be complete, it pleased the Father to forsake his well-beloved Son. Sin was laid on Christ, so God must turn away his face from the Sin-Bearer. To be deserted of his God, was the climax of Christ’s grief, the quintessence of his sorrow. See here the distinction between the martyrs and their Lord; in their dying agonies they have been divinely sustained; but Jesus, suffering as the Substitute for sinners, was forsaken of God. Those saints who have known what it is to have their Father’s face hidden from them even for a brief space, can scarcely imagine the suffering that wrung from our Savior the agonizing cry, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?</sty>”

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">47.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Some of them that stood there, when they heard that, said, his man calleth for Elias.</sty>

[BODY] A person in such agony as Jesus was suffering might have mentioned many pangs that he was enduring; but it was necessary for him to say, “I thirst,” in order that another Scripture might be fulfilled. <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">One of them,</sty> more compassionate than his companions, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">ran, and took a spurge, and filled it with vinegar,  </sty>from the vessel probably brought by the soldiers for their own use, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink.  </sty>It always seems to me very remarkable that the sponge, which is the very lowest form of animal life, should have been brought into contact with Christ, who is at the top of all life. [BODY] Thus didthe material world pay homage to him whom man had rejected; while nature’s convulsions foretold what will happen when Christ’s voice once more shakes not the earth only, but also heaven.

[BODY] These first miracles wrought in connection with the death of Christ were typical of spiritual wonders that will be continued till he comes again,— rocky hearts are rent, graves of sin are opened, those who have been dead in trespasses and sins, and buried in sepulchres of lust and evil, are quickened, and come out from among the dead, and go unto the holy city, the New Jerusalem.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">54.</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">  </sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">Now when the centurion, and they that were with him, watching Jesus, saw the earthquake, and those things that were done, they feared greatly, saying, Truly this was the Son of God.</sty>

[BODY] These Roman soldiers had never witnessed such scenes in connection with an execution before, and they could only come to one conclusion about the illustrious prisoner whom they had put to death: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Truly this was the Son of God</sty>.” It was strange that those men should confess what the chief priests and scribes and elders denied; yet since their day it has often happened that the most abandoned and profane have acknowledged Jesus as the Son of God while their religious rulers have denied his divinity.

[CENTERED] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">“</sty><sty c="000000" i="1" b="1">What makes a doctrine straight and clear? About five hundred pounds a year,</sty><sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">”</sty>

[BODY] <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">And this saying is commonly reported among the Jesus unto this day.  </sty>This lie, which had not a leg to stand upon, lived on till Matthew wrote his Gospel, and long afterwards. [BODY] The modern philosophy, which is thrust forward to cast a slur upon the great truths of revelation, is no more worthy of credence than this lie put into the mouths of the soldiers; yet common report gives it currency, and amongst a certain clique it pays.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">16, 17.</sty><sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">  Then the eleven disciples went away into Galilee, into a mountain where Jesus had appointed them. And when they saw him, they worshipped him: but some doubted.</sty>

[BODY] Notice those words, <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">the eleven disciples.  </sty>There were twelve; but Judas, one of the twelve, had gone to his own place; and Peter, who had denied his Lord, had been restored to his place among the apostles. The eleven <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">went away into Galilee,  </sty>to<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>the trysting-place their Lord had fixed: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">into a mountain where Jesus had appointed them.  </sty>Jesus always keeps his appointments, so he met the company that assembled at the selected spot: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">and when they saw him, they worshipped him.  </sty>Seeing their Lord, they began to adore him, end to render divine honors to him, for to them he was God: <sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">but some doubted.  </sty>Where will not Mr. Doubting and other members of his troublesome family be found? We can never expect to be quite free from doubters in the Church, since even in the presence of the newly risen Christ “some doubted.” Yet the Lord revealed himself to the assembled company, although he knew that some among them would doubt that it was really their Lord who was risen from the dead.

[BODY] Probably this was the occasion referred to by Paul, when the risen Savior “was seen of above five hundred brethren at once.” It was evidently a meeting for which he had made a special appointment, and his own words to the women, following those of the angel, seem to point this out as the one general assembly of his Church on earth before he ascended to his Father. Those who gathered were, therefore, a representative company; and the words addressed to them were spoken to the one Church of Jesus Christ throughout all time.

[BODY] <sty c="000000" i="0" b="1">18-20.</sty> <sty c="800000" i="1" b="1">And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.</sty>

[BODY] What a truly royal speech our King made to his loyal subjects! What a

--- PAGE 509 ---

[BODY] contrast was this scene in Galilee to the groans in Gletheemane and the gloom of Golgotha! Jesus claimed omnipotence and universal sovereignty: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>This is part of the reward of his humiliation (Philippians 2:6-10). On the cross he was proclaimed King of the Jews; but when John saw him, in his apocalyptic vision, “on his head were many crowns,” and on his vesture and on his thigh he had a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.

[BODY] By virtue of his kingly authority, he issued this last great command to His disciples: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Go ye therefore, and teach</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>or, “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">make disciples of all nations, baptising them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>This is<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>our commission as well as theirs. From it we learn that our first business is to make disciples of all nations, and we can only do that by teaching them the truth as it is revealed in the Scriptures, and seeking the power of the Holy Spirit to make our teaching effective in those we try to instruct in divine things. Next, those who by faith in Christ become his disciples are to be baptized into the name of the Triune Jehovah; and after baptism they are still to be taught all that Christ commanded. We are not to invent anything new; nor to change anything to suit the current of the age; but to teach the baptized believers to observe “all things whatsoever” our Divine Thing has commanded.

[BODY] This is the perpetual commission of the Church of Christ; and the great seal of the Kingdom attached to it, giving the power to execute it, and guaranteeing its succens, is the King’s assurance of his continual presence with his faithful followers: “<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.</sty>”<sty c="800000" i="1" b="0">  </sty>May all of us realize his presence with us until he Call us to be with him, “for ever with the Lord”! Amen.
